## Summary

Add a pane-launch capability to the shared herdr plugin code — ContextHub `packages/herdr/shared/` (consumed by other Herdr plugins (e.g. in open_source_llm) via the `packages/ContextHub` git submodule). When launching a new pane the operator chooses between:

- **Add to the right** — plain herdr split-right, no resizing (herdr default behavior).
- **Add to a resizing group** — open the pane on the right AND rebalance the right side into an even grid (2 columns, filled top-to-bottom; the anchor/current pane keeps 50% width × 100% height).

**Default: add to a resizing group.**

## User Stories

- As an operator launching a new pane, I want the pane to open on the right and existing panes to rebalance into an even grid automatically, so my workspace stays tidy without manual resizing.
- As an operator, I want an explicit opt-out (`--no-resize`, "add to right") that uses herdr's default split-without-resizing behavior.
- As an operator, I want the resizing-group behavior to work when panes are added one at a time without knowing the final count in advance, so I can build a grid incrementally.

## Proven Algorithm (validated against herdr 0.7.5)

- Wire protocol: newline-delimited JSON-RPC over the herdr Unix socket (`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`); `{"id","method","params"}`.
- Growth policy (even-completion): at odd k split the bottom-left cell DOWN; at even k split the bottom-right cell DOWN; then rebalance all split ratios via `layout.set_split_ratio` (boolean path arrays; `True` = second child).
- Tree invariant: `root:right [anchor, S1]`; `S1:down [R1, B]`; `B:right [L_col, R_col]`; each column is a down-chain (paths `[T,T,F...]` / `[T,T,T...]`). Both chains share the same denominator base `max(len(L), len(R))` so row boundaries align; at odd k the shorter (right) column's last cell spans two bands.
- Verified shapes: k=12 → 6×2, k=14 → 7×2; odd counts show a temporary tall cell that completes at the next even addition.
- Reference implementations: `/tmp/dynamic_grid.py` (build from scratch) and `/tmp/grid_step.py` (add to an existing grid), plus `/tmp/herdr_rpc.py` (socket helper).

## Constraints (from testing)

- **NEVER use `layout.apply` with `command` nodes — it kills panes.** Even `layout.apply` referencing only existing pane IDs kills those panes and creates fresh ones. `pane.move` only works across tabs/workspaces; `pane.swap` does not change tree shape. In-place restructuring is therefore impossible — the tree shape is fixed by the growth policy.
- Use only safe operations: `pane.split`, `layout.set_split_ratio`, `pane.rename`, `pane.close`.

## Suggested Implementation

- **No new script**: extend the existing shared launch scripts `send-to-pi.sh` and `open-pi-agent.sh` with a `--resize` (default) / `--no-resize` flag pair.
  - `--resize` (default) — split right AND rebalance the right side into an even grid (anchor keeps 50% × 100%)
  - `--no-resize` — plain herdr split-right, no layout changes (today's behavior)
  - `--pane-name`, `--focus`/`--no-focus`, `--cwd`, `--model` — unchanged from existing shared scripts
- Add a Python helper `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` (socket JSON-RPC over `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`): determine grid state (anchor + L_col/R_col chains) from the herdr session snapshot; growth policy (odd k → split bottom-left cell down; even k → split bottom-right cell down); rebalance split ratios via `layout.set_split_ratio`.
- The bash scripts resolve the anchor pane (`herdr pane current`), invoke `grid.py` (which performs the split and prints the new pane id), then launch/rename/focus the pane as today.
- Add tests: Python unit tests (mocked socket) for grid-state transitions and emitted JSON-RPC messages/ratios; bash tests (mock herdr CLI) for both scripts' mode handling.
- If `grid.py` fails, the script exits non-zero with a clear message (operator can retry with `--no-resize`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The existing shared launch scripts (`packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/open-pi-agent.sh`) gain `--resize` (default) and `--no-resize` modes (no new script)
- [ ] `--no-resize` performs a plain herdr split-right with no layout changes (herdr default)
- [ ] `--resize` opens the pane on the right and rebalances the right side into an even grid (verified: k=12 → 6×2, k=14 → 7×2; odd k → one temporary tall cell)
- [ ] The anchor/current pane is never split and keeps 50% × 100%
- [ ] Only safe operations are used (`pane.split`, `layout.set_split_ratio`); no `layout.apply` with `command` nodes
- [ ] Tests cover the grid-state transitions and emitted JSON-RPC messages

## Related

- related-to:WL-0MS8XGSE400374VS (Migrate ContextHub herdr plugin to Rust — shared Rust helper modules)
- related-to:OSL-0MS6D6MVW007ZRC2 (Extract shared Herdr plugin code between ContextHub and open_source_llm)
- Shared structure design: docs/herdr-code-inventory.md (open_source_llm repo)

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` (new — grid rebalance helper)
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` (add `--resize`/`--no-resize`)
- `packages/herdr/shared/open-pi-agent.sh` (add `--resize`/`--no-resize`)
- `packages/herdr/shared/README.md` (document both modes)
- `packages/herdr/shared/tests/test_grid.py` (new — grid unit tests, mocked socket)
- `packages/herdr/shared/tests/test_scripts.sh` (new — bash tests, mock herdr CLI)

## Plan

### Feature breakdown (4 children)

1. **Grid-rebalance Python tests** (test) — pytest unit tests with a mocked socket: grid-state transitions at odd/even k, emitted JSON-RPC messages (`pane.split` direction/ratio, `layout.set_split_ratio` path arrays + ratios), verified shapes k=12 → 6×2 and k=14 → 7×2, temporary tall cell at odd k, anchor never split.
2. **Shared grid helper `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py`** (impl) — socket JSON-RPC client, grid-state detection (with fresh-grid fallback), growth policy, `layout.set_split_ratio` rebalance; safe ops only; prints the new pane id. Depends on 1.
3. **Shared script resize-mode bash tests** (test) — mock-herdr bash tests for `send-to-pi.sh` / `open-pi-agent.sh`: `--resize` default, `--no-resize` plain split with no grid calls, unchanged option parsing, grid.py invocation with anchor pane id, error handling.
4. **Resize mode in shared launch scripts** (impl) — add `--resize`/`--no-resize` to both scripts; resize mode resolves the anchor (`herdr pane current`) and invokes `grid.py`; update `shared/README.md`. Depends on 2 and 3.

Dependency edges: 2←1, 4←2, 4←3.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-04: Planned via plan skill. Decisions: (Q1) bash entrypoints + Python helper `grid.py`; (Q2) no new script — existing scripts gain `--resize`/`--no-resize`; (Q3) AC #6 dropped — herdr-podcast-editor is being removed. Description ACs, Suggested Implementation, and Related updated accordingly.

### Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Script structure & language — bash entrypoint + Python helper, pure Python, or pure bash?" Answer (operator, 2026-08-04): "you choose". Final: A — bash entrypoints (`send-to-pi.sh`, `open-pi-agent.sh`) + shared Python helper `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` for socket RPC and grid logic, consistent with the existing shared scripts and the validated Python reference implementations.
- Q: "Should send-to-pi.sh / open-pi-agent.sh be refactored to delegate through a new open-pane.sh?" Answer (operator, 2026-08-04): "We don't want a new script, we want existing scripts to use the new algorithm". Final: no new script; both existing scripts gain `--resize` (default) / `--no-resize`.
- Q: "Cross-repo consumer scope for AC #6 (herdr-podcast-editor launch flow)?" Answer (operator, 2026-08-04): "drop AC6 we are going to remove the podcast editor". Final: AC #6 removed from the parent; no consumer integration work in this item.

## Reference Implementations

The following validated reference implementations are embedded here so the implementer has everything without relying on /tmp files (which are ephemeral). They were tested against herdr 0.7.5 and produced the verified shapes in the ACs (k=12 → 6×2, k=14 → 7×2).

### herdr_rpc.py — minimal herdr socket RPC client

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal herdr socket RPC client."""
import socket, json, sys

SOCK = "/home/rgardler/.config/herdr/herdr.sock"

def rpc(method, params, timeout=5):
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    s.connect(SOCK)
    s.sendall(json.dumps({"id": "py-1", "method": method, "params": params}).encode() + b"
")
    s.settimeout(timeout)
    data = b""
    while True:
        chunk = s.recv(65536)
        if not chunk:
            break
        data += chunk
        if b"
" in data:
            break
    s.close()
    return json.loads(data.decode())

def layout(pane_id):
    return rpc("pane.layout", {"pane_id": pane_id})["result"]["layout"]

def show(pane_id, title):
    l = layout(pane_id)
    print(f"--- {title} ---")
    for p in l["panes"]:
        r = p["rect"]
        print(f"  {p['pane_id']}: x={r['x']} y={r['y']} w={r['width']} h={r['height']}")
    for s in l["splits"]:
        print(f"  split {s['id']}: {s['direction']} ratio={s['ratio']}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    pane = sys.argv[1]
    show(pane, "layout")
```

### dynamic_grid.py — build the grid from scratch (k=1..N)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Dynamically grow an even grid of panes to the right of a fixed left pane.

POLICY: complete rows at even counts.
  k=2r   -> r full rows x 2 cols  (perfect grid, e.g. k=12 -> 6x2)
  k=2r+1 -> r full rows + a tall cell in the bottom row (inherent to
            herdr's no-restructuring constraint; the next even addition
            completes the row and the grid is perfect again).

Tree model (verified against herdr's split ids):
  root: right [left, S1];  S1: down [R1, B]
  R1: right [a, b]                  (row 1)
  B:  right [L_col_root, R_col_root] (creates the 2 columns for rows 2+)
  L_col: down-chain [TTF, TTFT, TTFTT, ...]  (left column, rows 2..r)
  R_col: down-chain [TTT, TTTT, TTTTT, ...]  (right column, rows 2..r)
  The two chains use identical ratios so the row boundaries line up.

Growth (after k=4):
  odd k: split L_col[-1] down  (left column gains a cell; right stays tall)
  even k: split R_col[-1] down (right column gains a cell; row completes)

Usage: dynamic_grid.py <left-pane-id> [target-count]
"""
import sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp')
from herdr_rpc import rpc, layout

MY_PANE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "w1:p80"
TARGET  = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 12

def split(pane, direction, ratio):
    r = rpc("pane.split", {"target_pane_id": pane, "direction": direction,
                           "ratio": ratio, "focus": False})
    assert "result" in r, f"split failed: {r}"
    return r["result"]["pane"]["pane_id"]

def set_ratio(path, ratio):
    r = rpc("layout.set_split_ratio", {"tab_id": tab_id, "path": path, "ratio": ratio})
    assert "result" in r, f"set_split_ratio failed: {r}"

def rebalance(n_left, n_right):
    """n_left/n_right = number of cells in each column chain (rows 2+).
    The row bands are defined by the LONGER chain (the left one at odd k);
    the shorter chain must use the same denominators to stay aligned
    (its last cell goes tall at odd k).
    """
    base = max(n_left, n_right)
    rows = 1 + base
    set_ratio([True], 1.0 / rows)                    # S1
    set_ratio([True, False], 0.5)                    # R1 (row 1)
    if n_left >= 1 and n_right >= 1:
        set_ratio([True, True], 0.5)                 # B (2-column split)
    for j in range(n_left - 1):                      # L_col chain
        set_ratio([True, True, False] + [True] * j, 1.0 / (base - j))
    for j in range(n_right - 1):                     # R_col chain
        set_ratio([True, True, True] + [True] * j, 1.0 / (base - j))

tab_id = layout(MY_PANE)["tab_id"]
L_col, R_col = [], []
k = 0

for step in range(1, TARGET + 1):
    k += 1
    if k == 1:
        p2 = split(MY_PANE, "right", 0.5)
    elif k == 2:
        p3 = split(p2, "down", 0.5)
        set_ratio([True], 0.5)
    elif k == 3:
        p4 = split(p2, "right", 0.5)                 # R1 = [p2, p4]
        R_col = [p3]                                 # bottom wide row
        rebalance(0, 1)
    elif k == 4:
        p5 = split(p3, "right", 0.5)                 # bottom wide -> 2x2
        L_col = [p3]
        R_col = [p5]
        rebalance(1, 1)
    elif k % 2 == 1:                                 # odd: grow left column
        new = split(L_col[-1], "down", 0.5)
        L_col.append(new)
        rebalance(len(L_col), len(R_col))
    else:                                            # even: grow right column
        new = split(R_col[-1], "down", 0.5)
        R_col.append(new)
        rebalance(len(L_col), len(R_col))

    n = max(len(L_col), len(R_col))
    rows = [["*", "*"]] + [[L_col[i] if i < len(L_col) else None,
                              R_col[i] if i < len(R_col) else None] for i in range(n)]
    print(f"k={k:2d} -> rows={json.dumps(rows)}")

print(f"
FINAL k={k}: {1 + max(len(L_col), len(R_col))} rows x 2 cols (left pane 50%)")
```

### grid_step.py — add N panes to an EXISTING grid

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Continue growing an EXISTING even-completion grid (Pattern B).

State must be a perfect even grid (k = 2 + len(L) + len(R), len(L) == len(R)).
Usage: grid_step.py <left-pane> <L_col-ids> <R_col-ids> [extra-panes]
  e.g. grid_step.py w1:p80 w1:pAS,w1:pAW,w1:pAY,w1:pA0,w1:pB2 \
                    w1:pAV,w1:pAX,w1:pAZ,w1:pB1,w1:pB3 1
"""
import sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp')
from herdr_rpc import rpc, layout

MY_PANE = sys.argv[1]
L_col = [x for x in sys.argv[2].split(',') if x]
R_col = [x for x in sys.argv[3].split(',') if x]
N = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 1

def split(pane, direction, ratio):
    r = rpc("pane.split", {"target_pane_id": pane, "direction": direction,
                           "ratio": ratio, "focus": False})
    assert "result" in r, f"split failed: {r}"
    return r["result"]["pane"]["pane_id"]

def set_ratio(path, ratio):
    r = rpc("layout.set_split_ratio", {"tab_id": tab_id, "path": path, "ratio": ratio})
    assert "result" in r, f"set_split_ratio failed ({path}): {r}"

def rebalance(n_left, n_right):
    """n_left/n_right = number of cells in each column chain (rows 2+).
    The row bands are defined by the LONGER chain (the left one at odd k);
    the shorter chain must use the same denominators to stay aligned
    (its last cell goes tall at odd k).
    """
    base = max(n_left, n_right)
    rows = 1 + base
    set_ratio([True], 1.0 / rows)                    # S1
    set_ratio([True, False], 0.5)                    # R1 (row 1)
    if n_left >= 1 and n_right >= 1:
        set_ratio([True, True], 0.5)                 # B (2-column split)
    for j in range(n_left - 1):                      # L_col chain
        set_ratio([True, True, False] + [True] * j, 1.0 / (base - j))
    for j in range(n_right - 1):                     # R_col chain
        set_ratio([True, True, True] + [True] * j, 1.0 / (base - j))

tab_id = layout(MY_PANE)["tab_id"]
k = 2 + len(L_col) + len(R_col)
for _ in range(N):
    k += 1
    if k % 2 == 1:                                   # odd: grow left column
        new = split(L_col[-1], "down", 0.5)
        L_col.append(new)
    else:                                            # even: grow right column
        new = split(R_col[-1], "down", 0.5)
        R_col.append(new)
    rebalance(len(L_col), len(R_col))
    print(f"k={k}: L_col={len(L_col)} R_col={len(R_col)} (new={new})")

print(f"
FINAL k={k}: {1 + max(len(L_col), len(R_col))} bands on the right")
```

### Live session example (how the grid was built and verified)

Built in tab `w1:t3G`, anchor pane `w1:p80`:

```
$ python3 /tmp/dynamic_grid.py w1:p80 12
k= 4 -> rows=[["*", "*"], ["w1:pAS", "w1:pAV"]]            # 2x2
k= 6 -> rows=[["*", "*"], ["w1:pAS", "w1:pAV"], ["w1:pAW", "w1:pAX"]]   # 3x2
...
k=12 -> 6 rows x 2 cols  (perfect grid)

$ python3 /tmp/grid_step.py w1:p80 \
    w1:pAS,w1:pAW,w1:pAY,w1:pA0,w1:pB2 \
    w1:pAV,w1:pAX,w1:pAZ,w1:pB1,w1:pB3 2
k=13: L_col=6 R_col=5 (new=w1:pB4)   # 6 rows + tall cell
k=14: L_col=6 R_col=6 (new=w1:pB5)   # 7x2 perfect grid
```

## Summary

Investigate what circumstances lead to a work-item being placed into the 'Other' group in the herdr plugin selection list, and improve the grouping rules so items no longer fall into 'Other'.

data.title: Herdr plugin: eliminate the 'Other' group in the selection list by improving grouping rules

data.description:
# Herdr plugin: eliminate the 'Other' group in the selection list by improving grouping rules

## Problem statement

The herdr work item selection list renders a section labeled `Other` for any non-critical work item whose stage is not one of `plan_complete`, `intake_complete`, `idea`, or `in_review`. In practice this bucket is filled by **`in_progress` items** — actionable work that is actively being implemented. These items are arguably the most actionable in the list, yet they currently appear in a vague "Other" section instead of the actionable `Group N` lists. The goal is that **no item should ever land in "Other"** in normal operation; "Other" should remain only as a safety net for genuinely unknown/custom stages or stale stage/status combinations.

## Users

- **Herdr users** browsing the Worklog Selection List pane (default "next" worklist).
  - *As a user, I want in-progress items (work currently being implemented) to appear at the top of the actionable `Group N` lists, so I can see at a glance what is actively being worked on.*
- **`wl next` CLI users** who see grouped output (`-n N` with group headings).
  - *As a CLI user, I want in-progress items grouped with other actionable work (`Group N`), not under a catch-all "Other" heading.*
- **Pi TUI users** browsing the worklog browse list (same grouping algorithm). *(Note: the Pi TUI browse extension — `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/grouping.ts` — was removed from the repo on 2026-08-06 by `Remove the Pi-based TUI from the repo; keep the agent-side Pi plugin features (WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N)`; the herdr plugin is now the sole TUI browsing surface, so only two grouping copies remain.)*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`in_progress` joins Group N**: Non-critical items with stage `in_progress` are partitioned together with `plan_complete`/`intake_complete` items by file-path conflicts into the existing `Group N` lists (no stage prefix in the label; same greedy first-fit algorithm). Verified by unit tests in all three grouping copies.
2. **In-progress items sort at the top within their group**: Within every file-path group (`Group N` and `Critical Group N`), items sort by stage sub-order `in_progress` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining stages, then priority (high → medium → low). Verified by ordering tests.
3. **"Other" is empty for all canonical stages**: With the change, no item with a canonical stage (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_progress`, `in_review`, `done`) lands in "Other" in the default herdr selection list (note: `done` items are already excluded from the default list by smart selection). "Other" remains only as a safety-net fallback for unknown/empty/custom stages.
4. **Both remaining copies stay in sync**: `src/commands/grouping.ts` (core `wl next`) and `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (herdr plugin) are updated consistently, per the documented keep-in-sync decision (Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B). The third copy (Pi TUI extension `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/grouping.ts`) was removed from the repo on 2026-08-06 by WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N and is out of scope.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/FILE_PATH_CONVENTION.md` "When to Include" table and "Group display order" section).
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The herdr plugin and Pi TUI extension have **zero npm dependencies** and cannot import from `src/commands/` — each maintains a deliberate copy of the grouping algorithm. All three copies must be kept in sync manually (documented decision Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
- Do not remove the "Other" catch-all entirely — it is the safety net for unknown/custom stages (user decision).
- Do not change the existing `Critical Group N` partitioning for critical items; only their within-group sort order gains the `in_progress`-first sub-order (shared ordering constant).
- Group labels and the group display order (`Critical Group N` → `Group N` → `Idea` → `Other` → `In Review`) are unchanged; only the membership of `Group N` and the within-group ordering change.

## Existing state

`assignItemGroups()` in all three copies assigns:
- `Critical Group N` — priority `critical` (any stage), partitioned by file-path conflicts.
- `Group N` — non-critical `plan_complete` + `intake_complete`, partitioned by file-path conflicts.
- `Idea` — non-critical stage `idea`.
- `Other` — everything else non-critical (currently: `in_progress`, `done`, unknown/empty/custom stages).
- `In Review` — non-critical stage `in_review`, placed last.

Within-group sort (`WITHIN_GROUP_STAGE_ORDER`) is currently `plan_complete` (0) → `intake_complete` (1) → remaining (2), then priority.

Live data (ContextHub worklog, 2026-08-01): `wl next --include-in-progress` returns 30 items; the only items landing in "Other" are the 3 non-critical `in_progress` items (e.g. `Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced (WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR)`, `a-y (audit approve) shortcut does nothing (WL-0MS95CEAE0080EB4)`, `Quality Improvement - Refactoring (WL-0MS87KJZU006XM5M)`). Both the core `wl next` CLI output and the herdr regrouped list render them under `── Other ──`. Stages in use across the worklog: `done`, `idea`, `in_progress`, `in_review`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`.

## Desired change

1. In `assignItemGroups()` (all three copies), include non-critical `in_progress` items in the `Group N` membership filter (alongside `plan_complete` and `intake_complete`).
2. In the `WITHIN_GROUP_STAGE_ORDER` constant (all three copies), insert `in_progress: 0`, shifting `plan_complete` → 1 and `intake_complete` → 2. This makes in-progress items sort ahead of plan_complete within every file-path group (both `Group N` and `Critical Group N`), which is consistent and desirable since in-progress work is actively being worked.
3. Keep "Other" as-is as the safety-net fallback (now effectively only for unknown/empty/custom stages; `done` remains excluded from the default list by smart selection).
4. Update affected tests (see Key Files) and docs; verify no regressions.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — Core `assignItemGroups()` + `WITHIN_GROUP_STAGE_ORDER`; add `in_progress` to Group N membership and stage sub-order.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — Herdr plugin copy of the same algorithm (must stay in sync). Also update its file-header comment, which still references the removed Pi TUI copy (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/grouping.ts`).
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — Several tests use `in_progress` items as the canonical "Other" example; update to the new expectations and use a truly-unknown stage (e.g. `undefined`/`'done'`) for "Other" coverage.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — Canonical group order test + In Review positioning regression test (WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW); in_progress item no longer lands in "Other".
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — In Review positioning regression test (WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW); uses an `in_progress` item (group 3, groupLabel "Other") to position the In Review section — update to a truly-unknown stage.
- `docs/FILE_PATH_CONVENTION.md` — "When to Include" table (`in_progress` → "**Should** include (groups items into `Group N`)") and "Group display order" section (Group N membership + within-group order).
- `src/commands/next.ts` — No logic change expected (it already consumes `assignItemGroups`/`compareGroupedItems`), but verify group headings render correctly.

## Related work

- `Improve group ordering and Other group behavior in selection list (WL-0MQWA8ZFN008GRKM)` — established the single "Other" group behavior and reversed ordering; later superseded by the rewrite below. Relevant for historical context on why "Other" exists.
- `Rewrite assignItemGroups + next.ts ordering (WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ)` — authored the current spec: Critical Group N → Group N (plan_complete + intake_complete) → Idea → Other → In Review. This work item refines that spec.
- `Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW)` — duplicate In Review sections fix; introduced `regroupWorkItems` in the herdr copy. The regression tests updated here stem from this item.
- `Herdr plugin regroup fix (WL-0MSAKPWIY005DL8W)` / `Pi TUI regroup fix (mirrored) (WL-0MSAKPXCD009I1CY)` — regroup fixes in both TUI copies.
- `Core grouping tests for new spec (WL-0MSAKPVD3001JL24)` — the grouping-utility tests updated by this work.
- `wl next --groups/-g not honoured when file paths have trailing description text (WL-0MR92SLZW001EH3Y)` — file-path extraction edge cases; relevant if in_progress items' paths mis-extract.
- `Add wl doctor stage-sync command to fix stale stage/status combinations (WL-0MQPS28DW008QFL3)` — data hygiene for stale stage/status (e.g. completed + in_progress), which "Other" still catches as a safety net.
- `docs/FILE_PATH_CONVENTION.md` — documents the current grouping rules and file-path convention.
- `Remove the Pi-based TUI from the repo; keep the agent-side Pi plugin features (WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N)` — removed the third grouping copy (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/grouping.ts` + tests) on 2026-08-06; this work item's description was updated to the two remaining copies.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The change applies to all three grouping copies (core `wl next`, herdr plugin, Pi TUI extension) to keep behavior consistent, per the documented keep-in-sync decision. The primary user-visible fix is the herdr selection list; core `wl next` CLI output changes identically.
- **Assumption:** Critical items with stage `in_progress` should also sort first within their `Critical Group N` (shared within-group ordering). Consistent with "in-progress work is actively being worked".
- **Risk — stale stage/status combinations:** An item with `status=completed` and `stage=in_progress` would now render in `Group N` rather than "Other". Mitigation: data hygiene via `wl doctor stage-sync`; acceptable in practice and noted.
- **Risk — tests relying on `in_progress` → "Other":** Several tests in both remaining copies' suites (`tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`) use `in_progress` as the canonical "Other" example; they must be updated to use a genuinely unknown stage. Missing any copy's tests would cause CI failures.
- **Scope-creep guard:** No changes to smart selection (`selectWorkItems`), `isMandatoryItem`, group labels, or the group display order. Extra opportunities (e.g. removing "Other" entirely, custom-stage validation) are tracked as separate work items, not this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What is 'the second list' of the herdr plugin? The plugin has a single worklist pane; the identical grouping logic exists in three copies (core `wl next`, herdr plugin, Pi TUI extension)."
  - Answer (user): "that's a typo should be 'selection' as in the single 'selection list'". Source: interactive reply.
  - Consequence: scope is the single herdr selection list; the three grouping copies are kept in sync per the documented decision (Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
- Q: "Where should `in_progress` items go? Recommendation was an explicit 'In Progress' group after Group N and before Idea."
  - Answer (user): "Can we keep in_progress items in the existing [Critical] Group N lists? If so put them at the top, ahead of plan_complete". Source: interactive reply.
  - Consequence: `in_progress` items join the existing file-path-partitioned `Group N` lists (shared with plan_complete/intake_complete); within-group stage sub-order becomes in_progress → plan_complete → intake_complete → remaining.
- Q: "Should 'Other' be removed entirely, or kept as a safety net for unknown/custom stages?"
  - Answer (user): "Keep as a safety net". Source: interactive reply.
  - Consequence: "Other" remains as the fallback for unknown/empty/custom stages and stale stage/status combinations; goal is that it is empty in practice for all canonical stages.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQJL1W3X0055WJH** – Auto-refresh the Pi TUI browse selection list every 5 seconds (completed)
- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO** – Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane (completed)
- **WL-0MSALIQJU0084V9U** – Herdr worklist: remove 'Sent ...' toast shown when dispatching commands to a pi pane (open)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/docs/workflow/validation-rules.md` — matched: group, list, rules, selection
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/plan/detection.py` — matched: group, list, rules, selection
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/validation/skill-refactoring-validation.md` — matched: list, plugin, rules, seed

## Summary

Create the test suite for the canonical `resolveWorklogRoot(startDir?)` function in `packages/shared`, porting the existing `findWorklogRoot` integration cases from `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` and adding new cases for the unified strategy. Test-first feature for WL-0MS7TQVK2001X4EG.

## Context

Canonical strategy (approved by producer, see parent WL-0MS7TQVK2001X4EG):

- Valid `.worklog/` = contains `config.yaml` OR `initialized` (worklog.db-only dirs are invalid)
- Walk up from `startDir`; nearest valid `.worklog/` wins (local-wins)
- Invalid `.worklog/` stops the walk UNLESS it is a worktree-container stub (contains `worktrees/` and no markers) or the current dir is inside `.worklog/worktrees/`
- Never walk past the nearest git repo root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, worktree-aware)
- Outside git, walk to filesystem root
- Not found returns `undefined` (strict)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vitest suite for `resolveWorklogRoot` exists under `packages/shared/src/` (e.g. `packages/shared/src/worklog-paths.test.ts`)
- The existing `findWorklogRoot` integration cases are ported, with validity markers updated from `worklog.db` to `config.yaml` where applicable
- New cases cover: config.yaml-only valid dir; initialized-only valid dir; worklog.db-only dir is INVALID (walk stops, returns undefined); invalid non-stub `.worklog/` in cwd stops the walk; worktree-container stub is skipped; invalid `.worklog/` inside `.worklog/worktrees/` is skipped; walk stops at the git repo root (nested repo with a valid parent-repo `.worklog/` returns undefined); `startDir` parameter is respected; filesystem-root termination without infinite loop
- Tests run from the repo root via vitest and pass (e.g. `npx vitest run packages/shared/src/worklog-paths.test.ts`)

## Minimal Implementation

- Create `packages/shared/src/worklog-paths.test.ts` with a temp-dir harness (mirroring the existing plugin test patterns: `mkdtempSync`, `process.cwd` spy, cleanup)
- Port each plugin scenario; adjust markers per the canonical validity rule
- Add the new edge-case tests listed above
- Run the suite and iterate until green

## Dependencies

- None (test-first: written before the implementation feature)

## Deliverables

- `packages/shared/src/worklog-paths.test.ts` (or equivalent location) — failing-first tests ready for the implementation feature

## Summary

In `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh`, the `--exec` wrapper mode is meant to keep a pane's process alive indefinitely when stdin is not a TTY and `HERDR_PANE_ID` is set. It does this with:

```bash
read -r _ < /dev/zero || true
```

Reading from `/dev/zero` never returns a newline (so `read` never completes) but data is always immediately available (so the read syscall never blocks). Bash therefore spins in a tight read/scan loop at ~100% CPU instead of blocking.

## Observed incident (2026-08-01)

A test-invoked pane wrapper (`run-in-pane.sh --exec 'exit 42' pane-123`) ran for **9h12m at 99.9% CPU** (551 CPU-minutes), and the invoking `vitest run` in ContextHub stayed hung for **23.5 hours** waiting for it. Load average on the 16-core host reached ~313. Killing the wrapper let the hung vitest run complete immediately.

## Expected behaviour

Blocking the pane process should consume ~0% CPU while keeping the pane open.

## Suggested fix

Replace the `/dev/zero` read with a genuinely blocking construct, e.g. `sleep infinity`, or block on a FIFO/pipe with no writers. Note `sleep infinity` is GNU-coreutils only; the script targets bash on Linux so it is acceptable, but confirm the project's portability constraints.

## Acceptance criteria

1. With `HERDR_PANE_ID` set and non-TTY stdin, the `--exec` wrapper stays alive but consumes ~0% CPU (verified over a few seconds).
2. The TTY stdin path (wait for Enter) still works unchanged.
3. Non-pane contexts (neither TTY nor `HERDR_PANE_ID`) still exit immediately with the command's status.
4. A regression test covers the non-TTY + `HERDR_PANE_ID` path and asserts CPU usage stays near zero.

# Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible

## Problem

Pi agent sessions continuously spawn `wl list` / `wl next` subprocesses even when the work-item selection list (browse pane) is not visible. Each `wl` invocation spawns a new Node.js process (~50 MB), and with 13 concurrent pi agents this produced **206 concurrent wl processes consuming ~17 GB RAM** and load averages of 150-225 on a 16-core host.

## Observed Evidence

- 13 `pi` agent processes running concurrently (4 min to 2.5 hours elapsed), each spawning dozens of `wl` subprocesses per minute
- Commands observed being respawned continuously:
  - `wl list --status open,in-progress,blocked --json`
  - `wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress --json`
  - `wl list --priority critical --root-only --json`
  - `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json`
  - `wl sync --if-idle`
- Killing the wl processes frees memory only temporarily — the pi agents respawn them within seconds
- The 206-count snapshot was during a period when no selection list interaction was happening (agents were idle/processing elsewhere)

## Hypothesis

The pi extension's work-item selection list (browse pane) polls `wl list` / `wl next` on a refresh cadence regardless of whether the pane is actually visible/rendered. When the pane is hidden or the user is working in another context, the polling continues unnecessarily. The `wl sync --if-idle` spawns may also continue per-agent even when not needed.

## Expected Behaviour

- If a selection list / browse pane is not visible, it must not poll `wl list` / `wl next`
- Polling should only run when the pane is rendered and being viewed
- `wl sync --if-idle` should not run when no visible pane requires fresh data

## Investigation Steps

1. Locate the pi extension code that drives the work-item selection list polling (likely in the browse/selection pane lifecycle)
2. Determine when the pane is created/destroyed and whether polling starts/stops with visibility
3. Confirm whether hidden panes or non-visible tabs keep polling
4. Identify the refresh cadence and why it fires when invisible

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When no work-item selection list is visible in a pi session, no `wl list` / `wl next` processes are spawned by that session
2. When the selection list becomes visible, polling resumes
3. `wl sync --if-idle` only runs when needed (visible pane requiring fresh data)
4. Measurable: with N idle pi agents and no visible selection lists, wl process count stays near 0
5. All existing tests pass

## Related

- discovered-from: WL-0MSB19J56006E87J (Investigate excessive wl process spawning)
- related-to: WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (Central cache for wl read results to cut Herdr refresh spawn churn)

# Tests — Idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget

## Summary

Test-first coverage for pausing the pi Worklog extension's 5-second auto-refresh (and auto-sync) while the browse selection widget is idle (no user keypresses within the idle threshold), so hidden or unused selection lists stop spawning `wl` processes.

## Context

Parent: Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N). Root-cause investigation (WL-0MSB19J56006E87J) confirmed the pi extension `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` `defaultChooseWorkItem` runs a 5s `setInterval` for the entire custom-widget session (`ctx.ui.custom(...)` until `done()`), regardless of user interaction or agent activity. Each tick spawns 4-5 wl processes (`next -n N --include-in-progress`, `list --priority critical --root-only`, `list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`, `list --status open,in-progress,blocked`, plus `wl sync --if-idle` via `_triggerAutoSync`) ≈ 60 spawns/min per mounted widget. `WL_PIMAN=1` auto-opens the browse flow on `session_start`, so every piman-launched pi session mounts the poller by default. This feature writes the tests for the idle-gating behavior.

## User stories

- As an operator with N idle pi sessions, I want the browse selection widget to stop polling when it has had no keypresses for the idle threshold, so wl process churn drops to ~0 while agents work elsewhere.
- As a user actively browsing work items, I want the list to keep auto-refreshing at the existing cadence while I interact, so I don't lose live updates.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New tests (in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.test.ts` or a new colocated test file) cover the idle-gated interval with fake timers; the fetcher is mocked so invocation counts are observable (no real `wl` spawns)
2. Tick within the idle window (interaction within `IDLE_PAUSE_MS`) → refresh fetch invoked (current behavior preserved while active)
3. Tick after the idle threshold (no keypresses for > `IDLE_PAUSE_MS`) → fetch NOT invoked (zero wl spawns)
4. Auto-sync trigger (`_triggerAutoSync`) is also skipped when idle
5. A keypress after an idle pause triggers an immediate refresh and resumes the cadence
6. Widget mount counts as interaction (freshly opened widget starts in active state)
7. Detail-view widget (which has no interval) is unaffected; manual actions (navigation, shortcuts, `r`/`S`-style refreshes) still work regardless of idle state
8. Tests run green: `npx vitest run packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.test.ts` (plus any new test file)

- Follow existing mock patterns in `browse.test.ts` (`vi.mock('@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent')`, mock `ctx.ui.custom` widget factory returning `{ render, invalidate, handleInput }`)
- Use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTime()` to drive the interval; mock the fetch path (e.g. `run`/`listWorkItems`) to count invocations
- Cover the resume-on-keypress path by calling the widget's `handleInput` after advancing time

## Dependencies

- None (test-first: precedes the implementation feature)

## Deliverables

- Test file changes under `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/`
- Green vitest suite demonstrating the idle-gating contract

# Impl — Idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget

## Summary

Implement idle-gated polling in the pi Worklog extension's browse widget: pause the 5s auto-refresh interval (and auto-sync) when the user has not interacted with the selection list for the idle threshold, resuming immediately on the next keypress.

## Context

Parent: Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N). The pi extension `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` `defaultChooseWorkItem` starts a 5s `setInterval` when the browse widget mounts and keeps it running for the entire custom-widget session, spawning 4-5 wl processes per tick (~60/min) even when the user is not interacting and the agent is working elsewhere. Pi's `resetExtensionUI()` (session rebind/reload) does not close custom sessions, so the poller survives those too. This feature gates the interval on user interaction.

## User stories

- As an operator with N idle pi sessions, I want hidden/unused selection lists to stop spawning wl processes, so wl process count and memory stay near zero while agents are idle or working elsewhere.
- As a user actively browsing, I want the list to keep refreshing live while I interact, so I don't lose real-time updates.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `browse.ts` tracks `lastInteractionAt` — set when the browse widget mounts and updated on every `handleInput` keypress
2. The 5s refresh interval skips the fetch (and `_triggerAutoSync`) when `Date.now() - lastInteractionAt > IDLE_PAUSE_MS` (named module constant, default 30_000ms)
3. First keypress after an idle pause triggers an immediate refresh and resumes the normal cadence
4. No new settings/config toggles (consistent with the pause-when-hidden decision: always-on, fail-open); the idle threshold is a named constant
5. Active cadence unchanged: while the user interacts, refresh continues at the existing interval
6. Zero wl subprocesses spawned while idle (verified by the A1 test suite plus manual process-count observation)
7. All A1 tests and existing `browse.test.ts` tests pass; the package build (`tsc` via `npm run build` in the extension package or repo build) succeeds

## Minimal implementation

- In `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` `defaultChooseWorkItem`: add `IDLE_PAUSE_MS` constant; record `lastInteractionAt` at mount and at the top of `handleInput`; in the interval callback, skip fetch + auto-sync when idle; on resume, invalidate cache and trigger an immediate fetch
- Leave the detail-view widget path and manual actions untouched
- Note (pi-side limitation, out of scope): pi's `resetExtensionUI()` doesn't close custom sessions — idle gating covers that case

## Dependencies

- Depends on the A1 test feature (test-first)

## Deliverables

- `browse.ts` changes implementing idle-gated refresh/sync
- Green test suite (A1 + existing) and successful build

# Wire showIcons setting and add settings reload mechanism for herdr worklog plugin

## Problem Statement

The `showIcons` setting is defined in the herdr worklog plugin settings (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`) and documented in the README, but it has **two issues**:

1. **showIcons is not wired into the renderer.** The `iconsEnabled()` function in `src/icons.ts` always returns `true` — it ignores the setting entirely. So editing `showIcons` in the config has no effect on whether icons appear in the list.
2. **No settings reload mechanism exists.** Several settings (`autoRefresh`, `refreshIntervalMs`, `autoSync`, `syncIntervalMs`) are read only once at startup in `main()`. After editing the config, the user must quit and reopen the pane for those settings to take effect.

## Root Cause Analysis

- `src/settings.ts` defines `showIcons: boolean` in `PluginSettings` and loads it from the JSON config file.
- `src/index.ts` calls `loadSettings()` but never passes `showIcons` to the TUI options.
- `src/worklist.ts` calls `iconsEnabled()` with no arguments — it always returns `true`.
- `src/icons.ts` `iconsEnabled()` has no connection to the settings file.
- `src/index.ts` reads settings once in `main()` and passes them to `runWorklistTui()`. No mechanism exists to re-read settings at runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **showIcons is wired into the renderer.** When `showIcons` is `false` in the config, no icons appear in the worklist (status, stage, priority, audit icons are all omitted). When `showIcons` is `true` (default), behavior is unchanged.
2. **showIcons changes apply without restart.** The setting is re-read from disk on every render/fetch cycle (same pattern as `showHelpText` and `browseItemCount`).
3. **Settings reload is properly implemented.** The pattern mirrors `showHelpText`: a `getShowIcons` getter function re-reads from disk on every call.
4. **Tests added.** Unit tests verify that `iconsEnabled()` respects the noIcons flag when passed, and integration tests (or at least a test) confirm the settings re-read path.
5. **Backwards compatible.** Default behavior is unchanged — icons are shown by default.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Wire showIcons through the TUI options

**Files: `src/index.ts`, `src/worklist.ts`**

- Add `showIcons` to the settings passed to `runWorklistTui()` (similar to `autoRefresh`, `refreshIntervalMs`, etc.)
- In `runWorklistTui()`, accept `showIcons` in the options and store a getter pattern like `getShowIcons: () => loadSettings().showIcons ?? true`
- Pass `noIcons` flag down to `renderWorklist()`

### Step 2: Update iconsEnabled() to respect the flag

**File: `src/icons.ts`**

- `iconsEnabled()` already accepts `{ noIcons?: boolean }` — it returns `false` when `noIcons === true`. This is correct; the bug is that callers never pass `noIcons: true`.
- **No changes needed here** — the function already works correctly when given the flag.

### Step 3: Pass noIcons through the render chain

**Files: `src/worklist.ts`**

- In the render function, replace `const noIcons = !iconsEnabled()` with the getter-based approach:
  ```ts
  const noIcons = !getShowIcons();
  ```
- Pass `noIcons` to `formatItemLine()` calls (already supported).

### Step 4: Add unit tests

**File: `src/settings.ts` or new test**

- Test that `showIcons: false` in config results in `noIcons: true`
- Test that the default value is `true`

## Key Files

- `src/settings.ts` — already loads `showIcons` from config
- `src/index.ts` — needs to pass `showIcons` to `runWorklistTui()` and add `getShowIcons` getter
- `src/worklist.ts` — needs to use the getter instead of always calling `iconsEnabled()` with no args
- `src/icons.ts` — already correct (accepts `noIcons` option)
- `src/icons.test.ts` — unit tests verifying `iconsEnabled()` respects the `noIcons` flag (AC4)
- `src/worklist.test.ts` — integration tests confirming the settings re-read path via the getter (AC4)

# Selection list refreshes immediately when its tab/pane regains focus

## Problem statement

The Worklog browse selection list pauses its 5-second auto-refresh after 30 seconds without keypresses (idle-gating added in WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N to stop hidden sessions spawning `wl` subprocesses). When the user switches to another terminal tab or tmux pane and returns, the list stays stale until the **first keypress** — if they just look at it, it does not update. The list should refresh immediately when the tab/pane it is displayed in regains focus, then resume the scheduled 5s cadence.

## Users

- **TUI users working in multiple tabs/panes** — they return to the Worklog browse pane and expect to see current data without pressing a key first.

User stories:
- _As a user running pi in tmux, I want the selection list to refresh immediately when I switch back to its pane, so I don't have to press a key to see fresh work items._
- _As a user who keeps the browse list open while working elsewhere, I want the list to resume its 5s refresh cadence as soon as its tab is focused again._

## Expected behaviour

1. While the browse widget is open, terminal focus reporting is enabled (DECSET 1004).
2. On focus-in (`\x1b[I`): the list re-fetches immediately and the 5s refresh cadence resumes (idle timer reset). This is the same refresh path already used by the "first keypress after idle" resume.
3. On focus-out (`\x1b[O`): no fetch; the existing idle-gating (no keypresses → pause after `IDLE_PAUSE_MS`) continues to apply, so hidden sessions still spawn zero `wl` subprocesses.
4. When the widget closes, focus reporting is disabled (DECSET 1004l) and the input listener is removed (no leaks).
5. Fail-open: terminals/tmux configurations that do not support focus reporting simply never send focus events — behaviour is unchanged from today (list resumes on first keypress after idle). No terminal should be negatively affected by the mode-set request (unsupported requests are ignored by terminals).

6. **Scope — tmux per-pane focus delivery:** tmux forwards focus events **only to the active pane**. If the Herdr/browse pane is *not* the active pane, it receives no focus-in/out events, so tab-level focus changes do **not** reach it. The immediate-on-focus refresh therefore fires when the browse pane itself is activated (click, `Ctrl+b` + arrow), not when a containing tab regains focus while another pane holds focus. The staleness indicator (WL-0MSBVCMNO00503QM) covers the UX for that case.

## Feasibility (verified during intake)

- pi-tui does **not** enable focus reporting today (no `\x1b[?1004h` is sent and no focus-in/out sequence handling exists).
- The extension **can** do it without framework changes:
  - The `custom()` UI factory receives the `TUI` object, which exposes `terminal` as a public field → `tui.terminal.write('\x1b[?1004h')` / `'\x1b[?1004l'`.
  - `onTerminalInput` (already in the browse `BrowseUi` interface) wires to the TUI input listeners, which receive raw data **before** the focused component; `\x1b[I` (focus-in) and `\x1b[O` (focus-out) are complete CSI sequences that pass through the stdin buffer.
- Constraints / caveats:
  - **tmux**: focus events are only forwarded with `set -g focus-events on` in `~/.tmux.conf` (document in README/settings help).
  - **Terminal support**: xterm, Kitty, Ghostty, WezTerm, iTerm2, Windows Terminal support focus reporting; others ignore the request (fail-open).
  - This detects OS/terminal-level tab/pane focus. Inside pi, the browse list always has input focus while open (it replaces the editor), so no intra-pi focus handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Sending focus-in (`\x1b[I`) to the open browse widget while idle triggers an immediate re-fetch and resumes the 5s cadence (unit test with fake timers / injected input).
2. Sending focus-out (`\x1b[O`) does not trigger a fetch.
3. Focus reporting is enabled on widget open (`\x1b[?1004h` written to terminal) and disabled on widget close (`\x1b[?1004l`), with the input listener unregistered (no listener/interval leaks across consecutive browse sessions).
4. Fail-open verified: with no focus events delivered (unsupported terminal), existing idle-gating behaviour is unchanged — the first keypress after idle still refreshes, and idle sessions spawn zero `wl` subprocesses (existing browse-idle tests continue to pass).
5. New tests cover the focus-in/out handling; full project test suite passes.
6. Documentation updated (README or in-extension help) noting the tmux `set -g focus-events on` requirement for focus-based refresh.

## Constraints

- Must not regress the idle-gating from WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N (zero `wl` subprocesses when the pane is hidden/idle).
- No changes to the pi framework (`/usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/`) — the fix must live in the Worklog extension (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/`).
- Keep the implementation minimal: re-use the existing idle-resume refresh path; do not add a new fetch mechanism.

## Existing state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` — `defaultChooseWorkItem` runs a 5s `setInterval`; the fetch is skipped when `isIdle()` (> `IDLE_PAUSE_MS` = 30s since last keypress); `handleInput` does an immediate refresh when the first keypress follows an idle pause.
- `BrowseUi` interface already declares `onTerminalInput?: (handler: TerminalInputHandler) => () => void`.
- `browse-idle.test.ts` covers the idle-gating behaviour.

## Desired change

In `defaultChooseWorkItem` (and its `_done` cleanup):
1. On widget open: `tui.terminal.write('\x1b[?1004h')` (guard with `typeof tui.terminal?.write === 'function'`) and register an `onTerminalInput` listener that detects `\x1b[I` → immediate re-fetch + `lastInteractionAt = Date.now()` (same path as the idle-resume refresh); `\x1b[O` → no-op.
2. On `_done` (widget close): `tui.terminal.write('\x1b[?1004l')` and unregister the listener.
3. Extend the `BrowseUi.custom` type (or the widget factory signature) as needed so the terminal write is type-safe.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts` — focus reporting enable/disable, focus-in listener, immediate-refresh hook, cleanup in `_done`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse-idle.test.ts` — new tests for focus-in/out behaviour (or a new `browse-focus.test.ts`).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/README.md` (or in-extension help) — document tmux `set -g focus-events on` requirement.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (completed, in_review): introduced the 30s idle-gating this item refines.
- **WL-0MQJL1W3X0055WJH** — Auto-refresh the Pi TUI browse selection list every 5 seconds (completed): the 5s cadence.
- **WL-0MSBVCMNO00503QM** — Show staleness indicator in selection list when its refresh is paused (new, related): fallback UX when focus detection is unavailable.
- **WL-0MKVTLJJP07J4UKR** — Add TUI refresh shortcut (completed): precedent for refresh UX.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Focus reporting may not be forwarded in all environments (tmux without `focus-events on`, terminals without support). Mitigation: fail-open; the fallback staleness-indicator item (WL-0MSBVCMNO00503QM) covers the UX gap in those environments.
- **Risk:** The `\x1b[?1004h` mode-set could theoretically interfere with another application's handling of the terminal. Mitigation: only enabled while the browse widget is open, disabled on close; unsupported terminals ignore it.
- **Assumption:** `tui.terminal` is accessible from the custom widget factory at runtime (public field on `TUI`). Verify against the actual `TUI` type during implementation; if inaccessible, fall back to writing via `process.stdout` guarded by mode.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Intra-pi focus (e.g., "widget vs editor focus") is out of scope — the list always holds input focus while open; only OS/terminal-level tab/pane focus is addressed.

# Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus (hidden→visible transition)

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist TUI pauses its auto-refresh when its tab is hidden (visibility gating via `herdr pane get <id>` → `pane.focused === false`, WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N). When the tab regains focus, the list only refreshes on the **next regular refresh tick** — up to `refreshIntervalMs` (default 30s) later. Users returning to the tab wait silently for the list to catch up, and cannot tell it will update at all. The list should refresh **immediately** on the hidden → visible transition, then resume the normal cadence.

## Users

- **Herdr users running multiple panes/tabs** — they switch away from a tab containing a work-item list and return expecting current data immediately.

User stories:
- _As a user with three panes in a tab where the Herdr list is not the focused pane, I want the list to refresh as soon as the tab regains focus, so I don't wait up to 30s for the next tick._
- _As a user returning to a long-hidden tab, I want the refresh to happen immediately and the paused indicator to clear right away._

## Expected behaviour

1. While the pane is hidden (`pane.focused === false`), refresh/sync ticks continue to be skipped (zero `wl` spawns — unchanged).
2. The plugin detects the **hidden → visible transition** (visibility state flips false → true) and triggers an immediate `doRefresh()` on that transition — not waiting for the next regular `refreshIntervalMs` tick.
3. After the transition refresh, the normal scheduled cadence resumes.
4. The transition is detected promptly: while paused, visibility is polled on a short interval (e.g. 2s, matching `DEFAULT_POLL_GATE_TTL_MS`) instead of only on the 30s refresh tick. The poll uses `herdr pane get` only — never `wl` — so the no-wl-when-hidden guarantee from WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N is preserved.
5. The existing `[paused — hidden]` header indicator clears as soon as the list refreshes after becoming visible.
6. Fail-open unchanged: when visibility cannot be determined (no `HERDR_PANE_ID`, CLI error), polling proceeds as today.

## Implementation notes

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — in `runWorklistTui`, track the previous visibility state alongside `panePaused`. In the refresh timer tick: if hidden → record `wasHidden = true`, skip; if visible and `wasHidden` → call `doRefresh(true)` (immediate, with the "refreshed" notification) and clear `wasHidden`; else normal tick behaviour.
- Prompt transition detection: while `panePaused`, run a lightweight resume poll (e.g. a 2s interval calling the existing `paneGate.visible()` — memoized by `PollGate`, one `herdr pane get` exec per poll) that flips to an immediate refresh the moment visibility returns. Stop the resume poll once visible; only the normal refresh timer runs.
- Keep the `PollGate` TTL (`DEFAULT_POLL_GATE_TTL_MS = 2000`) aligned with the resume poll interval so visibility state is never cached stale for longer than the poll.
- Tests: extend `worklist-visibility.test.ts` (inject `setExecFileAsync` seam; fake timers) for: (a) hidden → visible transition triggers an immediate fetch outside the normal tick; (b) while hidden the resume poll does not call the fetcher; (c) after the transition refresh, the cadence returns to `refreshIntervalMs`; (d) the header indicator clears.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — transition detection, immediate refresh on resume, resume poll while paused.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — possibly export a `PollGate` constructor variant with a shorter TTL for the resume poll (or reuse existing).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-visibility.test.ts` — new tests for transition + resume poll + cadence return.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a hidden pane becomes visible, the list re-fetches **immediately** (outside the regular `refreshIntervalMs` tick) — asserted with injected fetcher + fake timers.
2. While hidden, no `wl` fetches occur and the resume poll spawns only `herdr pane get` (no fetcher calls).
3. After the immediate transition refresh, subsequent refreshes follow the normal `refreshIntervalMs` cadence.
4. The `[paused — hidden]` header indicator clears once the transition refresh completes.
5. Fail-open preserved: no `HERDR_PANE_ID` / CLI error → behaves as today (no regression in existing visibility tests).
6. Full herdr package test suite passes (`packages/herdr`).

## Constraints

- Must not regress the zero-`wl`-spawn-when-hidden behaviour (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N).
- No changes to the external herdr app/framework (the `herdr` CLI is the calling framework; `herdr pane get` output shape is a given).
- The visibility signal stays tab-level (`pane.focused`); active-pane-level focus (which pane in a tab has the cursor) is out of scope — the transition fix covers the tab-hidden case regardless of which pane is active.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N** — Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible (completed, in_review): introduced visibility gating (`visibility.ts`, `PollGate`, paused header indicator).
- **WL-0MSBVBXEA0011OWF** / **WL-0MSBVCMNO00503QM** — closed (not needed): alternative focus-reporting and staleness-indicator approaches for the pi `/wl` browse extension; superseded by this item's use of herdr's own tab-level visibility signal.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `pane.focused` flips false → true reliably when the tab regains focus while the pane itself is not the active pane. The visibility.ts comment ("a hidden (non-focused) tab reports focused === false") supports tab-level semantics; verify with a live herdr session during implementation.
- **Risk:** The 2s resume poll adds one `herdr pane get` exec every 2s per hidden pane. Mitigation: this is the same lightweight CLI already polled every 30s while hidden; make the resume poll interval a named constant/setting if churn concerns arise; never route it through `wl`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Detecting "the active pane within a focused tab" (tmux-style pane focus) is out of scope; herdr's `focused` flag is tab-level and that is sufficient for the reported scenario.

## Problem

Each herdr worklist pane runs a refresh cycle every `refreshIntervalMs` that spawns 4 wl processes (`wl next`, `wl list --priority critical --root-only`, `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`, `wl list --status open,in-progress,blocked`). `doRefresh` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` has **no in-flight guard**: if a refresh cycle is still awaiting its wl calls when the next interval tick fires (common under load — a single `wl list` can take ~18s wall on a contended host), cycles overlap and wl processes pile up. `doSync` already has a single-flight mechanism (`--if-idle`/timer guard); `doRefresh` does not.

Identified during investigation WL-0MSB19J56006E87J (excessive wl process spawning, 206 concurrent / ~17 GB RAM). Related: WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E (sync-side lock storm), WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (central read cache).

discovered-from:WL-0MSB19J56006E87J

## User story

As a herdr user, I want the worklist pane to skip a refresh tick while the previous refresh is still running, so that refresh cycles never overlap and wl processes cannot accumulate during load.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `doRefresh` skips (or coalesces) a tick when the previous refresh cycle has not yet completed — no overlapping wl spawn bursts from a single pane.
2. No UI regression: a skipped tick does not leave the list stale forever; the next tick or a manual refresh still updates it.
3. A test verifies that two rapid consecutive refresh triggers produce at most one in-flight wl spawn set (single-flight behavior).
4. Existing herdr test suite passes; build succeeds.
5. Verified that pane refresh returns to normal cadence after the in-flight cycle completes.

## Suggested approach

Add a module-level or instance-level `isRefreshing` flag (or promise-based coalescing) set at the start of `doRefresh` and cleared in `finally`. If set on tick, return early (or schedule one trailing refresh). Mirror the existing `doSync` guard pattern in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` / `auto-sync.ts`.
data.title: Herdr worklist: add in-flight guard to doRefresh to prevent overlapping refresh cycles

## Problem

The excessive wl process spawning incident (WL-0MSB19J56006E87J: 206 concurrent wl processes, ~17 GB RAM) was detected only after it caused severe load (150–225 on a 16-core host). No lightweight mechanism exists to detect wl process accumulation early. The investigation report (docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md, §6) proposes a health check mechanism.

discovered-from:WL-0MSB19J56006E87J

## User story

As an operator, I want a lightweight watchdog that alerts when the number of concurrent wl processes exceeds a threshold for a sustained period, so that process accumulation is detected before it degrades the host.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `scripts/wl-process-healthcheck.sh` exists and counts node `wl`/worklog CLI processes (`ps`-based, no external deps).
2. Alerts when count exceeds a threshold (default 50) for 3 consecutive checks; logs the count to `/tmp/wl-healthcheck-count` on OK/Watch levels.
3. Emits an alert with the process tree (`ps -eo pid,ppid,etime,args`) when sustained high counts are detected; non-zero exit code on alert.
4. CI regression gate: after the test suite, assert zero orphaned `tsx src/cli.ts` processes remain (covers the WL-0MSB447TJ000R3N8 fix).
5. README/docs note added with usage (cron/systemd timer, 5-min cadence).

## Suggested approach

- Follow the script template in docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md §6.1.
- Add CI assertion as a small vitest or shell step in the repo's CI config (or a post-test hook in package.json).
- Thresholds: OK < 20, Watch 20–50, Alert > 50 sustained.
data.title: wl process health check watchdog (scripts/wl-process-healthcheck.sh + CI regression gate)

Add support for free-form prompts injected into a new pi agent pane from the herdr plugin chord shortcut system.

## Problem Statement

The herdr worklist plugin shortcut system (src/shortcuts.json) can open a new pi agent pane only when the shortcut command starts with one of three prefixes: `/skill:`, `/intake`, or `/plan` (see isAgentCommand() in src/index.ts). Any other command text — including an arbitrary user prompt like 'Review this code' — is routed to the stdout/pane channel and executed as a shell command instead of being injected into a fresh pi instance. There is no way to bind a chord to 'open a new pi instance and inject a custom prompt'.

## User Stories

- As a herdr worklist user, I want to press a chord that opens a new pi agent pane with my custom prompt pre-injected, so that I can kick off arbitrary agent work without typing it in pi manually.
- As a plugin maintainer, I want the routing extension to be minimal and covered by tests, so that existing shortcut routing behavior (agent vs pane vs stdout) is preserved.

## Expected Behaviour

1. A new agent-command prefix `/prompt:` is recognized by routeCommand()/isAgentCommand() in src/index.ts and routes to the agent channel (send-to-pi.sh), the same as /skill:, /intake, /plan.
2. When the command starts with `/prompt:`, the prefix is stripped before the remainder is passed to send-to-pi.sh, so pi receives only the prompt text (e.g. `pi "Review the current work item and suggest next steps"`), not the routing prefix.
3. A shortcut entry is added to src/shortcuts.json using the `/prompt:` prefix with a free chord (e.g. `o-p`), view both, with a descriptive label.
4. The claim-work-item step (claimItemForAgentCommand) still runs safely for /prompt: commands: commands without a work-item ID skip the status update; commands containing a work-item ID token still claim it, matching existing agent-command behaviour.
5. Existing routing behaviour is unchanged: /skill:, /intake, /plan still route to agent; !! / ! commands still route to pane; unprefixed commands still route to stdout.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `routeCommand('/prompt:Some prompt text')` returns `'agent'`.
2. The /prompt: prefix is stripped before spawning send-to-pi.sh (unit-testable via an exported helper or verified in the routing integration).
3. `routeCommand('/skill:implement <id>')`, `routeCommand('/intake <id>')`, `routeCommand('/plan <id>')` still return `'agent'`; `routeCommand('!!wl close <id>')` still returns `'pane'`; `routeCommand('/wl idea')` still returns `'stdout'`.
4. shortcuts.json contains a `/prompt:` entry with a free chord (not colliding with existing chords: a-a, a-y, a-f, a-r, c, n, p, i, r, s, u-p-*, u-s, u-t, x-c, x-d, f-*).
5. `npm run build` in packages/herdr succeeds and `dist/shortcuts.json` contains the new entry.
6. All tests in packages/herdr pass (npm test), including new tests for /prompt: routing.

## Implementation Notes

- Files: packages/herdr/src/index.ts (isAgentCommand + agent branch prefix strip), packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json (new entry), packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts (new tests).
- The `!!`-prefixed wrapper-script alternative (option A) is explicitly out of scope.
- Related: existing herdr plugin work items (see wl search herdr).
data.title: Herdr plugin: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi pane (option B)

# Intake Brief: Add model to the shortcut keys

## Problem statement

Herdr's `shortcuts.json` dispatches commands to a pi agent pane, but there is no way to select which LLM model pi uses when executing those LLM-bound commands. Every agent command currently runs with whatever model pi happens to have selected, forcing the user to switch models manually per workflow.

## Users

Herdr users who drive Worklog workflows via keyboard shortcuts (intake, plan, implement, audit, free-form prompts) and want each workflow to run on an appropriately specialised model without manual model switching.

User stories:

- As a user pressing the implement shortcut, I want the command to run with the `code` model so implementation work runs on the code-specialised model.
- As a user pressing the plan/intake/audit shortcuts, I want commands to run with the default `plan` model.
- As a user invoking a free-form `/prompt:` shortcut, I want the new pi pane to open with the `author` model for writing tasks.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `ShortcutEntry` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` supports an optional `model` field, parsed and validated by `loadShortcutConfig`. When absent, the default is `plan`.
2. LLM-bound entries in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` carry explicit `model` values: `/plan`, `/intake` (both create and intake), and `/skill:audit` → `plan`; `/skill:implement` → `code`; `/prompt:` → `author`. Shell (`!!`) and `/wl` filter entries get no `model` field.
3. When an agent command with a model is dispatched, the pi CLI spawned via `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` is invoked with `--model <id>` (e.g. `pi --model code '/skill:implement <id>'`), via a new `--model` option on the shared script.
4. Commands without a `model` field, and non-agent routes (shell `!!` commands, `/wl` stage filters), are unaffected — no `--model` flag is passed.
5. Tests cover: config parsing of the `model` field (and defaulting), model propagation through chord dispatch → `onCommand` → agent routing, and `--model` flag forwarding in the send-to-pi.sh bash harness.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from the documentation criterion — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Scope:** herdr only (`packages/herdr/`). The TUI extension (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/`) is explicitly out of scope — leave it untouched.
- Model values are pi model patterns; bare ids (`plan`, `code`, `author`) match the Local Proxy models registered in `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (`pi --model` supports bare id patterns).
- Existing command strings in `shortcuts.json` must remain unchanged — the model rides alongside the command (config field → CLI flag), not inside the command text.
- The `pi` CLI flag is `--model <pattern>` (supports `provider/id` and optional `:thinking`).

## Existing state

- Herdr's `shortcuts.json` entries have: `chord`, `command`, `view`, optional `stages`/`label`/`description`. No `model` concept.
- Chord dispatch chain: `worklist.ts` `handleChordKey` → `registry.lookupChord()` (returns command string) → `chordState.resolvedCommand` → `executeResolvedCommand()` → `dispatchChordCommand()` → `resolveAndRouteCommand()` → `onCommand(resolvedCommand)`.
- `index.ts` `onCommand` routes: `agent` (`/skill:`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`) → `spawn(SEND_TO_PI_SCRIPT, ['--cwd', cwd, prompt])`; `pane` (`!!`/plain shell) → `run-in-pane.sh`; `stdout` → `CMD:` protocol.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` spawns the pane and runs `herdr pane run <np> exec pi "<command>"` — this is where the pi CLI invocation happens.
- `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` already mocks the herdr CLI to assert invocation args (used for `--cwd`); it is the natural home for `--model` forwarding tests.
- Models `plan`, `code`, `author` exist as ids under the "Local Proxy" provider in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`.

## Desired change

1. Add optional `model?: string` to `ShortcutEntry` and parse it in `loadShortcutConfig` (validate string, ignore non-strings), defaulting to `plan` for agent-bound commands without the field.
2. Add explicit `model` values to the LLM-bound entries in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`.
3. Propagate the model through the herdr dispatch chain so `onCommand` receives it (signature change: `(command, model?)` or entry-carrying lookup).
4. Add a `--model <pattern>` option to `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` that forwards `--model <pattern>` to the `pi` CLI invocation; pass it from `index.ts` for agent-route commands.
5. Update tests and documentation.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — add `model?: string` to `ShortcutEntry`; parse/validate in `loadShortcutConfig`.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — add `model` values to LLM-bound entries (`plan`/`code`/`author` as agreed).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — propagate model through chord dispatch, `executeResolvedCommand`, `dispatchChordCommand`, `resolveAndRouteCommand`, `onCommand`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the model to `send-to-pi.sh` for the `agent` route only.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — new `--model` option; pass `--model <pattern>` to the `pi` CLI.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/send-to-pi.sh` — passthrough wrapper (should need no change beyond forwarding args).
- Tests: `tests/herdr/shortcuts.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (agent-routing asserts), `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (dispatch chain).

## Related work

- `herdr /prompt: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi agent pane (WL-0MSC0O8HN000EBFH)` — established the agent channel / send-to-pi.sh path this feature extends.
- `Default config entries and child item updates (WL-0MQD1NPAD000O7OB)` — created the default `shortcuts.json` config; the file this feature extends.
- `Dynamic shortcut dispatcher for browse list (WL-0MQD1NEY7004366H)` — origin of the config-driven shortcut dispatch architecture.
- `~/.pi/agent/models.json` — registers the `plan`/`code`/`author` model ids under the Local Proxy provider (environment, not repo).
- pi docs `models.md` and `--model` CLI flag — model pattern semantics.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQP303A900780R0** – Escape key in Pi TUI work item detail view should navigate back to selection list (completed)
- **WL-0MKX5ZV3D0OHIIX2** – Add regression tests for mouse click crash and TUI behavior (completed)
- **WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL** – Recursive deletion of work items with children (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-add-model-to-the-shortcut-keys-WL-0MSD48ZFC0043AO3.md` — matched: add, also, author, code, commands, default, entries, executing, implement, item, json, keys, llm, model, models, once, plan, shortcut, shortcuts, should, want, when, writing
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MS5URWJG000A6O5-align-icons/packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — matched: able, add, also, code, commands, complete, default, define, entries, executing, implement, item, json, keys, model, models, once, plan, shortcut, shortcuts, when
- `CLI.md` — matched: able, add, also, author, centric, code, commands, complete, default, entries, going, implement, item, json, once, plan, should, similar, specified, want, when

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `pi --model <bare-id>` resolves the Local Proxy models correctly (bare-id pattern matching is documented; flag verified via `pi --help`).
- **Assumption:** default `plan` applies to any agent-bound command whose entry lacks a `model` field (per work item description).
- **Assumption:** invalid/unknown model ids surface as a pi startup/availability issue in the new pane rather than a herdr crash; config values are aligned with `models.json`.
- **Risk:** dispatch signature changes touch many call sites/tests — keep the change surgical (model as an additional optional parameter, defaulting to `plan`).
- **Scope creep risk:** TUI extension model support, model-cycle ordering, per-project model config, and model validation against `models.json` are all out of scope; create separate work items if requested.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should the model be applied when a shortcut fires? (a) extension calls `pi.setModel()` at dispatch; (b) editor text prefixed with `/model <id>`; (c) other?" — Answer (user@rgardler): "it should be in the pi cli command" — i.e., pass `--model <id>` on the `pi` CLI invocation when spawning the agent pane. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Scope: TUI extension only, or also `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`?" — Answer (user@rgardler): "herdr only, leave tui". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Proposed command→model mapping: `/plan`, `/skill:audit` → plan; `/skill:implement` → code; `/intake`, `/prompt:` → author?" — Answer (user@rgardler): "/intake should be plan otherwise agree". Final mapping: `/plan`, `/skill:audit`, `/intake` (both entries) → `plan`; `/skill:implement` → `code`; `/prompt:` → `author`. Source: interactive reply.
