# Add code_freeze field to herdr shortcuts.json to filter shortcut availability during code freeze

## Problem statement

Agents respect code freeze by refusing to start implementation work, but the herdr TUI's shortcuts.json has no way to declaratively hide shortcuts (e.g. `i` / implement) during a freeze. Users see the `i` key in help hints, press it, and then get the code-freeze dialog — a wasted keypress and poor UX. Shortcuts should be filtered out of the registry at load/lookup time when they are marked as blocked by code freeze.

## Users

- **Developers in the herdr TUI** — they should only see shortcuts that are actionable (no `i` visible during freeze).
- **Producers** — they need to know that certain shortcuts are intentionally hidden during freeze.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **`code_freeze` field parsed from shortcuts.json** — each entry may have `"code_freeze": "block"` (hide during freeze), `"code_freeze": "allow"` (always show), or omission (always show, backward compatible). Invalid values are logged and treated as omit.
- [ ] **Shortcut registry filters by freeze state** — `getEntriesForStage()`, `getChordByPrefix()`, and `lookupChord()` accept a `codeFreezeActive: boolean` parameter and exclude entries with `code_freeze: "block"` when frozen.
- [ ] **Shortcuts with `code_freeze: "block"` hidden from help hints** — chord hints and footer hints in the list view omit blocked shortcuts when freeze is active.
- [ ] **Implement shortcut blocked by default** — the `i` / `/skill:implement` entry in `shortcuts.json` gains `code_freeze: "block"` to hide it during freeze.
- [ ] **Tests pass** — new tests for the field parsing and registry filtering cover block/allow/omit cases.
- [ ] **Build passes** — `tsc` and full test suite (herdr only) pass.

## Constraints

- **herdr only** — no changes to the TUI extension (packages/tui).
- **Only implement shortcut affected for now** — the `i` chord gets `code_freeze: "block"`.
- **Fail-open** — missing file or parse error must not crash the registry or block other shortcuts.
- **Backward compatible** — existing entries without `code_freeze` behave unchanged.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` — detects freeze state from `<worklog-dir>/code-freeze.json` with fail-open semantics. Exports `isCodeFreezeActive()` / `readCodeFreezeState()`.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `ShortcutRegistry` with methods: `lookupChord()`, `getEntriesForStage()`, `getChordByPrefix()`, `getChordByLeader()`. `ShortcutEntry` has `chord`, `command`, `view`, `stages`, `label`, `description`.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `runWorklistTui()` computes `codeFreezeActive` via `readCodeFreezeState().active` and passes it to the renderer and keyboard dispatch paths.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — the config file defining shortcut entries. The `i` chord maps to `/skill:implement <id>`.
- `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.test.ts` — tests for code-freeze detection (not shortcut integration).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — Add `code_freeze` field to `ShortcutEntry` interface, update `loadShortcutConfig()` parser, update `getEntriesForStage()`, `getChordByPrefix()`, and `lookupChord()` to filter by freeze state.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — Tests for field parsing and registry filtering.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Add `code_freeze: "block"` to the `i` chord entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Pass `codeFreezeActive` to shortcut registry methods at render and dispatch call sites.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk** — operator said only implement for now; if later more shortcuts need freezing, the field is extensible.
- **TUI extension not affected** — TUI has no code-freeze detection; if TUI needs it later, that is a separate work item.
- **Field value enum** — only `"block"` and `"allow"` defined; omit = show. No validation beyond type check (fail-open on unknown value).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR** — Code Freeze epic: herdr plugin blocks implement actions (banner + dialog) during ship-it process (parent)
- **WL-0MSBUCG73003MV3S** — Implement: code-freeze detection, banner, implement-command blocking and dialog (herdr plugin)
- **WL-0MSBU4OBU005WJNB** — Cross-repo marker contract (SorraAgents ship/implement skills)
- **WL-0MQDUOK9K002QHJU** — Stage-based shortcut condition filters (previous shortcut-config work, same pattern to extend)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the new field use true/false or a string enum?" — Answer (Map): String enum: `"block"` = hide during freeze, `"allow"` = always show, omission = show.
- Q: "Which shortcuts should be blocked?" — Answer (Map): Only the implement shortcut (`i` / `/skill:implement`) for now.
- Q: "Should this also change the TUI extension?" — Answer (Map): No, herdr plugin only.
- Q: "Should intake/plan/audit be blocked too?" — Answer (Map): No, only implement for now.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQMFER5N003N1LL** – Chord-based stage filter shortcuts in TUI (completed)
- **WL-0MRSGMTYY0062WFJ** – wl audit-set should fail hard when audit text is not persisted (completed)
- **WL-0MM368S4W104Q5D4** – Fetch and cache issue event timelines (completed)

## Summary

Write pytest unit tests for the herdr even-completion grid rebalance algorithm **before** implementing `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py`. Tests use a mocked Unix socket — no live herdr session required.

Parent: Add pane-launch option to shared herdr code: add-to-right vs resizing group (resizing group default) (WL-0MSAPRMRH002S10O)

## Context

The algorithm is validated (herdr 0.7.5) and embedded as reference implementations in the parent description: `dynamic_grid.py` (build from scratch k=1..N), `grid_step.py` (add to an existing perfect grid), and `herdr_rpc.py` (socket RPC client). The grid helper must reproduce the same growth policy:

- Tree invariant: `root:right [anchor, S1]`; `S1:down [R1, B]`; `B:right [L_col, R_col]`; each column is a down-chain (paths `[T,T,F...]` / `[T,T,T...]`).
- Growth: at odd k split the bottom-left cell DOWN; at even k split the bottom-right cell DOWN; then rebalance via `layout.set_split_ratio` (boolean path arrays; True = second child).
- Rebalance: base = max(len(L_col), len(R_col)); S1 ratio 1/(1+base); R1 0.5; B 0.5 (when both columns exist); chain ratios 1/(base-j).

## User Stories

- As a developer, I want automated tests for the grid transitions so regressions in the growth policy or emitted ratios are caught without a live herdr session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tests run with pytest and pass without any herdr session or real socket (mocked socket server)
- [ ] Growth policy tested at odd and even k (e.g. k=12 → 6×2, k=14 → 7×2; odd k shows one temporary tall cell)
- [ ] Emitted JSON-RPC messages asserted: `pane.split` direction/ratio and `layout.set_split_ratio` path arrays + ratios
- [ ] Anchor pane never split and keeps 50% × 100% (asserted across transitions)
- [ ] Grid continuation tested: adding panes to an existing perfect grid completes rows at even counts

## Suggested Implementation

- Tests live in `packages/herdr/shared/tests/` (e.g. `test_grid.py`).
- Mock the Unix socket: an in-memory capture of sent newline-delimited JSON-RPC frames, returning fixture layout snapshots shaped like `pane.layout` results.
- Expected messages derived from the parent's embedded `dynamic_grid.py` / `grid_step.py` outputs (also in /tmp).
- Fixtures mirror the verified geometry: equal row heights, equal column widths, anchor 50% × 100%.

- [ ] Tests pass with no herdr session; a mock herdr binary captures invocations

- Stub grid.py (e.g. via `HERDR_GRID_BIN` env override or a PATH shim) to assert invocation arguments and return a fake pane id.

## Summary

Implement `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` — a Python helper for the herdr even-completion grid rebalance, used by the shared pane-launch scripts' `--resize` mode.

Parent: Add pane-launch option to shared herdr code: add-to-right vs resizing group (resizing group default) (WL-0MSAPRMRH002S10O)

## User Stories

- As an operator launching a new pane with resize mode, I want the pane to open on the right and existing panes rebalanced into an even grid automatically, so my workspace stays tidy without manual resizing.
- As an operator, I want the resizing-group behavior to work when panes are added one at a time without knowing the final count in advance, so I can build a grid incrementally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Newline-delimited JSON-RPC over the herdr Unix socket; `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` configurable (fallback to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/herdr/herdr.sock` / `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`); frames shaped `{"id","method","params"}`
- [ ] Detects existing grid state (anchor + L_col/R_col chains) from the `pane.layout` snapshot; falls back to starting a fresh grid from the anchor when the right side is not a recognisable grid
- [ ] Growth policy: odd k → split bottom-left cell DOWN; even k → split bottom-right cell DOWN; then rebalance via `layout.set_split_ratio` with boolean path arrays (True = second child)
- [ ] Reproduces the verified shapes k=12 → 6×2 and k=14 → 7×2 (validated against herdr 0.7.5)
- [ ] Anchor pane never split; keeps 50% × 100%
- [ ] Only safe operations: `pane.split`, `layout.set_split_ratio`; no `layout.apply` with `command` nodes
- [ ] Prints the new pane id as JSON on stdout (e.g. `{"pane_id": "..."}`) so the calling bash script can launch/rename/focus it
- [ ] Clear non-zero exit with a helpful message on socket failure or RPC error

## Suggested Implementation

- Port the parent's embedded `herdr_rpc.py` + `dynamic_grid.py`/`grid_step.py` into a single module: socket client, layout parser, grid-state detector, growth step, rebalance.
- CLI interface usable from bash, e.g. `grid.py <anchor-pane-id>` (add one pane to the existing grid, or start a fresh grid if none).
- Keep boolean path arrays exactly as validated.
- Depends on the grid tests (child: Grid-rebalance Python tests) being written first.

## Related

- Reference implementations embedded in the parent description: `dynamic_grid.py`, `grid_step.py`, `herdr_rpc.py` (also present in /tmp).

## Summary

Add `--resize` (default) / `--no-resize` to the existing shared launch scripts `send-to-pi.sh` and `open-pi-agent.sh`. In resize mode the script resolves the anchor pane and invokes `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py` (which performs the split and prints the new pane id) before launching/renaming/focusing the pane.

Parent: Add pane-launch option to shared herdr code: add-to-right vs resizing group (resizing group default) (WL-0MSAPRMRH002S10O)

## User Stories

- As an operator launching a new pane, I want the pane to open on the right and existing panes to rebalance into an even grid automatically (default), so my workspace stays tidy without manual resizing.
- As an operator, I want an explicit opt-out (`--no-resize`, "add to right") that uses herdr's default split-without-resizing behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `send-to-pi.sh` and `open-pi-agent.sh` both accept `--resize` / `--no-resize`; `--resize` is the default
- [ ] `--no-resize` behaves exactly as today: plain `herdr pane split --current --direction right`, no grid calls, no layout changes
- [ ] `--resize` resolves the anchor pane (`herdr pane current`), invokes `grid.py`, parses the returned pane id, then launches the pane (pi / command), renames and focuses it as today
- [ ] Existing options preserved with unchanged defaults: `--pane-name`, `--focus`/`--no-focus`, `--cwd`, `--model`, `--check-cli`
- [ ] If `grid.py` fails, the script exits non-zero with a clear message (operator can retry with `--no-resize`)
- [ ] `packages/herdr/shared/README.md` documents both modes and the grid helper
- [ ] All bash tests (child: Shared script resize-mode bash tests) pass

## Suggested Implementation

- Add flag parsing mirroring the existing `--no-focus` style in both scripts.
- Resize mode: `anchor=$(herdr pane current ...)`, then `python3 "$(dirname "$0")/grid.py" "$anchor"`; parse the pane id from its JSON output; proceed with the existing launch/rename/focus steps.
- `--no-resize` mode: current split logic unchanged.
- Update `shared/README.md` table and add a "Resize mode" section.

# Test suite for scripts/install-herdr.sh

## Summary

Vitest suite that executes the bash install script (`scripts/install-herdr.sh`) against temp directories, following the precedent of `tests/scripts/install-pi-extension.test.ts` (which runs the script via `execFileSync('bash', [scriptPath], ...)` with an overridden HOME). Covers config-insertion logic (idempotence, missing-file creation, existing-binding skip, `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` override) and failure modes (herdr missing on PATH, unwritable config).

## User story

"As a developer running the install script, I want tests that prove the herdr config keybinding is inserted exactly once (never duplicated), the file is created when missing, and the script never fails the build even when herdr is absent."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the script twice against a temp `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` leaves exactly one `[[keys.command]]` block for `worklog-selection-list.open-worklist` (idempotence).
- Running the script with a non-existent config path creates the parent directory and file, containing the exact TOML block:
  ```toml
  [[keys.command]]
  key = "prefix+l"
  command = "herdr plugin action invoke worklog-selection-list.open-worklist"
  description = "Open the Worklog work item selection pane in a new tab."
  ```
- Running the script against a config that already contains a `worklog-selection-list.open-worklist` binding skips insertion (no duplication).
- The script honours `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH`; the default `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` is untouched when the override is set (test with temp HOME).
- The script exits 0 and prints a warning when `herdr` is not on PATH (test by setting PATH without herdr).
- The script exits 0 and prints a warning when the config file/directory cannot be written (read-only temp dir).
- Insertion is correct when the existing config file lacks a trailing newline (block appended with a leading newline, no mangling).
- All tests live in `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` and run under the repo's existing vitest config (`npx vitest run tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts`).

## Minimal implementation

- Single vitest file `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` using `execFileSync('bash', [scriptPath])`, `fs.mkdtempSync`, and `os.tmpdir()` temp dirs.
- No fake-herdr stub: herdr link behaviour is not stubbed (rely on herdr's own idempotence, verified at runtime); only herdr-missing warn-and-continue is tested (Q2 answer).
- Helper to read the temp config file and assert block presence/count.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first; tests fail until `scripts/install-herdr.sh` exists — expected red state).

## Deliverables

- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts`

## Key Files

- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts`
- `scripts/install-herdr.sh` (target under test)

# scripts/install-herdr.sh — idempotent herdr integration installer

## Summary

Bash install script (following `scripts/install-pi-extension.sh` conventions: `set -euo pipefail`, clear echo output, tolerant of missing binaries) that (a) links the Worklog herdr plugin via `herdr plugin link packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` (resolved from repo root) and (b) inserts the `prefix+l` → `worklog-selection-list.open-worklist` `[[keys.command]]` block into the herdr config only if not already present. Wired into `npm run build` via a `postbuild` hook (see sibling work item for wiring/docs).

## User story

"As a developer installing the Worklog repo, when I run the install script, I want the herdr worklist plugin linked and its prefix+l shortcut registered in my herdr config without duplicate entries if I re-run it, so the worklist just works."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Script resolves the config path from `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` when set, else `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (same resolution herdr uses).
- Script creates the config parent directory and file when missing (file may start empty with just the inserted block).
- Script appends the exact `[[keys.command]]` block (`key = "prefix+l"`, `command = "herdr plugin action invoke worklog-selection-list.open-worklist"`, `description = "Open the Worklog work item selection pane in a new tab."`) only when a binding for `worklog-selection-list.open-worklist` is not already present (grep-based existence check on the command string).
- Script appends with a leading newline when the existing file lacks a trailing newline; no other edits to the config (no reordering, no comment changes).
- Script runs `herdr plugin link packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` (path resolved relative to repo root) when herdr is on PATH; re-link is safe/no-op (herdr's own idempotence, verified at runtime — Q2 answer).
- Script exits 0 with a warning when `herdr` is not on PATH (link skipped; config insertion still attempted) or when the config cannot be written — `npm run build` must not fail in CI/offline environments.
- Follows `install-pi-extension.sh` style: `set -euo pipefail`, `SCRIPT_DIR`/`REPO_ROOT` resolution, friendly echo output.
- All tests in `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` pass (green).

## Minimal implementation

- Single file `scripts/install-herdr.sh`:
  - Resolve `SCRIPT_DIR`/`REPO_ROOT` (same pattern as `install-pi-extension.sh`).
  - `CONFIG_PATH="${HERDR_CONFIG_PATH:-$HOME/.config/herdr/config.toml}"`.
  - `grep -qF 'worklog-selection-list.open-worklist'` existence check; if absent, `mkdir -p` the dir and append the block (leading newline when needed) via `printf`/`cat >>`.
  - `command -v herdr` guard; if present run `herdr plugin link "${REPO_ROOT}/packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml"`, else warn and continue.
  - Never exit non-zero on herdr-missing or write failure — warn to stderr and exit 0.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: Tests for install-herdr script behaviors (test-first; this feature turns those tests green).

## Deliverables

- `scripts/install-herdr.sh`

## Key Files

- `scripts/install-herdr.sh`
- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` (tests that must pass)

## Summary

The pane-launch grid feature (WL-0MSAPRMRH002S10O) is broken: launching a new pane in resize mode (the default) fails with 'Error: Could not resolve the current pane.'

## Root cause

Both shared launch scripts resolve the anchor pane with:

```bash
anchor="$("$herdr_bin" pane current --json 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"pane_id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
```

herdr 0.7.5's `pane current` does NOT accept `--json` (exit 2, 'unknown option: --json'); it emits JSON by default. Since stderr is suppressed, `anchor` is empty and the script exits 1 before any split. The plugin spawns the script detached with stdio ignored, so the user sees nothing happen when launching from a newly opened plugin pane (prefix+l).

The bash tests missed this because the mock herdr CLI accepts any arguments.

## Steps to reproduce

1. herdr 0.7.5 session; open the worklist plugin (prefix+l)
2. Trigger an agent command that launches a pi pane (e.g. /prompt: or a /skill: shortcut)
3. No pane opens; `herdr pane current --json` fails

## Fix

- Drop `--json` from the `pane current` call in packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh and packages/herdr/shared/open-pi-agent.sh
- Harden grid.py grid-state detection: unrecognisable layout shapes (anchor not resolvable) should fall back to a fresh right-split of the current pane instead of misbehaving
- Add bash test coverage asserting `pane current` is invoked without `--json`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `herdr pane current` is called without `--json` in both shared scripts
- [ ] Resize mode resolves the anchor and launches a pane in a live herdr 0.7.5 session
- [ ] grid.py falls back to a fresh right-split when the layout is not a recognised grid
- [ ] Bash tests and Python tests pass
data.title: Fix resize-mode anchor resolution: herdr pane current rejects --json

Test-first contract for the herdr downtime worker (parent WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K). Defines the complete unit-test matrix and mocked proxy fixtures that F2/F3 implementation features must satisfy. Follows the repo convention of a dedicated test-suite feature created before implementation features (cf. WL-0MQD1N3JD007B0FZ).

## User stories

- As a developer, I want a precise, pass/fail test contract for idle detection, threshold timing, dispatch selection, single-flight, endpoint-failure handling and blocked-questions handling so implementation features have unambiguous Definition of Done.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` exists with mocked `fetch` fixtures for `GET /llama/local/status` covering: idle (all slots free), busy (active query / model switch / local lease), ambiguous (total_slots 0 or missing fields), and network error/timeout responses.
- [ ] Idle-detection tests: the worker is idle only when llama_server_running is true, no active query, no model switch, no active local lease, and `available_slots >= total_slots` with `total_slots > 0`; N=0 (default) means all slots free; N>total_slots never dispatches; ambiguous responses are busy.
- [ ] Threshold-timing tests (fake timers): idle duration must reach `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` continuously before dispatch; any busy poll resets the idle-since timestamp.
- [ ] Dispatch-selection tests: `wl next --stage intake_complete` → `/skill:plan <id>`; fallback `--stage idea` → `/skill:intake <id>`; no items → no dispatch; both `wl next` calls mocked.
- [ ] Single-flight tests: no second dispatch while one is in flight; dispatch consumes the slot (subsequent polls busy) so a new dispatch requires another full idle period.
- [ ] Endpoint-failure tests: errors/timeouts/HTTP failures are treated as busy and never throw or crash the worker.
- [ ] Blocked-questions tests: the dispatched prompt contains the instruction to record questions in a comment and set `--needs-producer-review true` then stop.

## Summary

Implementation feature for WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K. Adds the six downtime settings with defaults/clamps to the herdr worklist plugin and implements the single-flight poller for `GET /llama/local/status` with fail-closed parsing.

## User stories

- As an operator, I want to configure downtime behaviour (enabled, idle threshold, required free slots, poll interval, proxy URL, model) in `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` without a plugin restart.
- As a developer, I want a poller that treats endpoint failures as busy so the plugin never crashes or hammers the proxy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New settings keys in `settings.ts` with defaults: `downtimeEnabled` (true), `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` (240000), `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` (0 = all slots), `downtimePollIntervalMs` (30000, floor 10000 via `clampDowntimePollInterval`), `downtimeProxyUrl` (http://192.168.0.199:8000), `downtimeModel` (`plan`). Load/merge/clamp covered by unit tests.
- [ ] `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` semantics: 0 = all slots free required; any positive integer N is accepted and validated against total slots at runtime (N > total → never idle).
- [ ] Poller (`downtime-worker.ts`): GET `{proxyUrl}/llama/local/status` on `downtimePollIntervalMs`; single-flight (no overlapping polls); per-poll timeout (fail closed).
- [ ] Fail-closed parsing: HTTP errors, timeouts, network failures, invalid JSON, missing/ambiguous fields are treated as busy (no dispatch) and never throw or crash the plugin.
- [ ] Idle condition implemented per F1 contract: llama_server_running true, no active query, no model switch, no active local lease, `available_slots >= total_slots` with `total_slots > 0`. When `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` N is 0→all free; N < total slots without per-slot data → all slots free (fail closed, never "any N slots"); N > total → never idle.
- [ ] Settings are re-read each poll/tick so changes apply without a plugin restart.
- [ ] F1 poller/idle-detection/settings-clamp tests pass; full suite green at repo root (`npx vitest run`).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `PluginSettings` + `defaultSettings` + load/merge in `settings.ts`; add `clampDowntimePollInterval` and any other clamps.
- `downtime-worker.ts`: `fetchLocalStatus(url, timeoutMs)` with AbortSignal timeout; `evaluateIdle(status, requiredFreeSlots): boolean` (pure, testable); poll-loop scaffold with single-flight flag.
- Wire settings through `loadSettings()` calls; no independent setInterval yet (F4 integrates into the consolidated scheduler).

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL (test suite contract).
- Parent: WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K.

- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new keys + defaults + clamps
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — poller + idle evaluation (new)

## Summary

Implementation feature for WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K. Tracks continuous idle duration against `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` and, on threshold expiry, dispatches a visible pi agent pane: `wl next --stage intake_complete` → `/skill:plan <id>`, falling back to `--stage idea` → `/skill:intake <id>`. Includes the pre-dispatch claim, single-flight guard, and blocked-questions prompt instruction.

## User stories

- As an operator, when the local LLM has been idle for the configured threshold, I want the backlog to advance automatically: a visible (non-focus-stealing) pi agent pane runs /skill:plan on the next intake_complete item, or /skill:intake on the next idea item.
- As an operator, when an automated skill run needs answers I haven't given, I want the questions recorded on the work item and the item flagged for producer review so nothing blocks silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Idle-duration tracker: `idleSince` timestamp set on first idle poll, advanced each consecutive idle poll; any busy poll resets it; dispatch fires only when idle duration ≥ `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` continuously (AC1/AC5).
- [ ] Dispatch selection: run `wl next --stage intake_complete --json` → first item → `/skill:plan <id>`; if empty, `wl next --stage idea --json` → `/skill:intake <id>`; if both empty, no dispatch (wait for next idle period).
- [ ] **Tier fallthrough on CLI error**: when the `intake_complete` lookup fails (`ok: false`), the `idea` lookup is STILL performed; a tier-3 candidate dispatches `/skill:intake`. A tier-2 error followed by a genuinely empty tier 3 is fail-closed to busy (no dispatch, no cooldown — the backlog is not provably empty).
- [ ] **Three-strike rule on CLI errors**: three consecutive `wl-error` dispatch outcomes enter the no-candidate cooldown (full pause, no dispatch) AFTER logging the persistent error to the rolling downtime log via `deps.recordError`. Any successful dispatch or genuine no-candidate outcome resets the strike counter; a single transient error does not pause the worker; `dispatch-in-flight` is neutral (no strike).
- [ ] Item is claimed before dispatch (`wl update <id> --status in_progress`) so it appears in_progress immediately and a second pane's `wl next` cannot select it (cross-pane serialization decision Q5: no lock file).
- [ ] Dispatch via shared `send-to-pi.sh`: `--no-focus`, `--cwd <wlRoot>`, `--model <downtimeModel>`, pane name `Downtime plan`/`Downtime intake`; spawn detached and unref'd like existing dispatches.
- [ ] Single-flight: at most one dispatch in flight per plugin process; no dispatch before the idle threshold; after a dispatch the worker does not dispatch again until another full idle period (dispatch consumes the local slot → proxy busy).
- [ ] Blocked-questions handling: the dispatched prompt appends the instruction — "If you cannot proceed because you need answers from the operator, record the questions in a comment on the work item and run `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review true`, then stop." (AC6).
- [ ] F1 dispatch-selection / single-flight / blocked-questions / threshold-timing tests pass; full suite green at repo root (`npx vitest run`).

## Minimal Implementation

- `downtime-worker.ts`: `IdleTracker` (idleSince, recordPoll(isIdle), isThresholdMet(now)); `selectNextItem(wlNextFn)`; `buildDispatchPrompt(command, itemId)`; `dispatch(sendToPiArgs)` using `spawn` + claim via `wl update`.
- `dispatchDowntimeWork`: always attempt the `idea` lookup after a non-candidate/errored `intake_complete` lookup (tier fallthrough).
- `createDowntimeWorker`: consecutive-error strike counter (`DOWNTIME_ERROR_STRIKE_LIMIT = 3`); on the 3rd consecutive `wl-error` outcome call `deps.recordError(...)` then enter the no-candidate cooldown; reset the counter on dispatched / no-candidate / cooldown expiry. Expose the counter as a readonly getter for tests.
- New dep `DowntimeWorkerDeps.recordError(event)` — fail-closed, must never throw; wired in `createDowntimeDeps` (index.ts) to `appendDowntimeLogEntry` (rolling `.worklog` log).
- Prompt is passed directly to send-to-pi.sh (worker does not route through the TUI's routeCommand).

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-0MSG80254005ZNE9 (settings + poller).
- Parent: WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K. Related: WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX (no-candidate cooldown mechanism reused for the three-strike pause).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — tracker, selection, dispatch
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — tests
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — deps wiring (recordError → rolling log)

## Summary

Implement `src/read-cache.ts` — an on-disk read cache for the wl CLI at `~/.cache/wl/` (XDG cache dir), keyed by (worklog-dir, full argv, wl version), serving JSON-mode results only. Freshness is WAL-aware (watches `worklog.db` + `worklog.db-wal` + `worklog.db-shm`), bounded by TTL (30–60s), and safe under concurrent readers/writers (atomic temp-file + rename). This is option A (primary) from the parent item WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 and the tracer-bullet slice: module + unit tests, before CLI wiring (F2).

## User Experience Change

No user-visible change on its own. This establishes the cache substrate that F2 wires into the read commands; the observable win (fewer `wl` process spawns, lower load) lands with F2+.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Cache entry key is a deterministic hash of (absolute worklog-dir, full argv, wl version); different dirs or arg variants never collide (key collisions / arg-variant separation covered by tests).
2. Freshness is WAL-aware: a write touching `worklog.db`, `worklog.db-wal`, or `worklog.db-shm` invalidates the affected entries; write-then-read returns fresh data immediately (parent AC #2).
3. Entries expire after TTL (default 30–60s, configurable); stale entries are never served; cache is bounded (size/LRU purge).
4. Concurrent readers/writers across processes never corrupt the cache; writes are atomic (temp file + rename); no partial entries readable.
5. Unit tests cover: invalidation under WAL-mode write, key collisions, arg-variant separation, TTL staleness, concurrent access — all pass.

## Implementation Approach

- Implement `src/read-cache.ts`:
  - XDG cache dir resolution (`~/.cache/wl/`, honoring `XDG_CACHE_HOME`).
  - Cache-key hash from (resolved absolute worklog-dir, full argv, `WORKLOG_VERSION` from `src/version.ts` — guards schema drift across wl upgrades).
  - DB-state fingerprint: mtime+size of `worklog.db`, `worklog.db-wal`, `worklog.db-shm`; cheap content fingerprint fallback for coarse-mtime filesystems. Store the fingerprint in the entry header; compare on read.
  - `get`/`set` with atomic temp-file + rename; per-key concurrency safety; TTL check on read; bounded purge (access-time LRU) to prevent unbounded key growth.
- Write tests first (TDD) in `tests/read-cache.test.ts` per the parent's AC #6 (WAL-mode invalidation, collisions, arg variants, concurrency).
- Document cache layout + invalidation semantics in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

## Dependencies

None (foundational slice).

## Deliverables

- `src/read-cache.ts` (new module)
- `tests/read-cache.test.ts` (new test suite)
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section on cache layout/invalidation

## Summary

Wire the F1 read cache into the wl CLI: route `list`, `next`, `show`, `search`, and `status` (JSON mode only) through cache lookup/backfill in `src/cli.ts`; write commands bypass the cache and invalidate affected entries; add env-gated spawn instrumentation so the ≥60% spawn-reduction target (parent AC #7) can be measured and verified.

## User Experience Change

Herdr panes and pi-agent polling stop spawning redundant `wl` processes for byte-identical queries: repeat reads within the invalidation window are served from the shared cache. Refresh cadence stays 30s; nothing user-visible changes except lower system load and faster repeat queries.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Repeat identical JSON queries for `list`, `next`, `show`, `search`, `status` are served from cache without spawning a new `wl` process (parent AC #1; verified via spawn instrumentation).
2. Write commands (`create`, `update`, `close`, `delete`, `comment`, `dep`, `import`, `sync`) are never served from cache; an identical read immediately after a write returns fresh data (parent AC #3).
3. Full argv participates in the cache key: `--status open` vs `--status completed`, `-n 1` vs `-n 5`, `--include-in-progress`, `--root-only` variants all produce separate, non-colliding entries (parent AC #4).
4. Write-byproducts of read commands are accounted for: `next`'s auto re-sort and FTS index builds count as writes (invalidate), so cached `next`/`search` results stay sound.
5. Spawn-counter instrumentation (env-gated, e.g. `WL_SPAWN_COUNT`/log line) records `wl` process spawns; a simulated 6-pane refresh issuing identical queries shows ≥60% fewer spawns vs baseline (parent AC #7).

## Implementation Approach

- Cache lookup/backfill around read-command dispatch in `src/cli.ts`; JSON mode only (all real consumers — herdr, pi agents, audit scripts — use `--json`; text output is terminal/env-dependent and non-deterministic).
- Explicit invalidation on write-command paths (belt-and-braces atop the F1 DB-fingerprint detection).
- Env-gated spawn counter; reuse patterns from `src/wl-integration/spawn.ts` (WL-0MP15AM1N001OBII) where relevant.
- CLI integration tests in `tests/cli/`: key collisions, arg-variant separation, write-invalidation freshness, concurrent access; plus a baseline-vs-cached spawn report for AC #5.

## Dependencies

- F1: Read-cache core module with WAL-aware invalidation (WL-0MSGAE35E001557V) — the module and unit tests must land first.

## Deliverables

- `src/cli.ts` + `src/commands/{list,next,show,search,status}.ts` wiring
- Spawn instrumentation
- CLI integration tests + spawn-reduction report

## Summary

Option E from the parent item WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3: (1) a successful `wl sync` explicitly invalidates the read cache for that worklog dir so post-pull/merge reads are always fresh, and (2) a per-worklog-dir sync heartbeat (marker file with last-success timestamp) lets herdr auto-sync skip spawning `wl sync` entirely when one succeeded recently — cutting the remaining redundant sync spawns across panes.

## User Experience Change

With 6 panes on one worklog dir, only the first pane's auto-sync tick spawns `wl sync` per heartbeat window instead of all 6; sync-triggered data refreshes never show stale cached reads. No user-visible behavior change otherwise (sync cadence and semantics unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After a successful `wl sync`, identical reads return post-pull data (no stale cache served).
2. With 6 panes on one worklog dir, only the first spawns `wl sync` within the heartbeat window; the other 5 skip without spawning a process (measured).
3. Failed or skipped syncs do not refresh the heartbeat; heartbeat age + TTL bound staleness (no indefinite skip).
4. Tests cover heartbeat skip logic and sync→cache invalidation.

## Implementation Approach

- In `src/commands/sync.ts` (or `src/sync.ts`): on successful sync, invalidate the F1 read-cache entries for the worklog dir and write the heartbeat marker (dir, timestamp).
- In `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts`: before spawning `wl sync`, check the heartbeat age for the target worklog dir and skip when fresh. Retain the existing per-process single-flight guard; extend with cross-instance coordination.
- Tests: sync→invalidation in `tests/`; heartbeat skip in herdr auto-sync tests (mock spawn, verify no spawn when heartbeat fresh).

- F1: Read-cache core module with WAL-aware invalidation (WL-0MSGAE35E001557V) — cache invalidation API needed.
- F2: Wire read commands through cache (WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA) — cache must be live in the CLI before sync invalidation matters.

## Deliverables

- `src/commands/sync.ts` / `src/sync.ts` invalidation + heartbeat write
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` heartbeat-aware skip
- Tests for both behaviors

## Problem

The generic md viewer (OSL-0MSDYOVP6005T1X5, commit acc4246b) does not render episode `.podcast.md` files. Repro: open the worklist (`prefix+l`), open item **irish-folklore-fine-tuning (OSL-0MSG82DKE002LOYM)** — the detail view shows only the raw description; no `Episode file (md viewer)` section.

## Root cause (two stacked issues)

1. **Wrong base dir (ContextHub plugin):** `readKeyFile` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` resolves Key Files paths against `process.cwd()`, which for herdr plugin panes is the plugin source dir (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr` — confirmed via `herdr pane list`: every "Work Items" pane has `cwd=.../packages/herdr`), NOT the worklog root. The code comment claims "the process CWD when the plugin runs in a pane" is the worklog root — that is false; the real root is in `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` (used by `configureWorklogTarget`).
2. **Data-side convention (open_source_llm):** even relative to the worklog root (`/home/rgardler/projects/open_source_llm`), the item key path `irish-folklore-fine-tuning/irish-folklore-fine-tuning.podcast.md` does not exist — the file is at `.llm-wiki/wiki/podcast/irish-folklore-fine-tuning/irish-folklore-fine-tuning.podcast.md`. The migration script `migrate_paragraph_format.py` (line 472/533) writes `Key Files:` paths relative to the podcast dir (`.llm-wiki/wiki/podcast`), while the documented convention (`docs/pipeline-metadata-format.md` §2.7) is relative to the wiki root.

Verified: `resolve(pluginCwd, keyPath)` -> false; `resolve(wlRoot, keyPath)` -> false; `resolve(wlRoot, ".llm-wiki/wiki/podcast/" + keyPath)` -> true.

## Proposed fix

- Plugin: resolve Key Files md paths against the resolved worklog root (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` / `wlRoot`), not `process.cwd()`; consider fallback candidates (worklog root, `.llm-wiki/wiki/podcast/`) so existing podcast-relative paths work.
- Data (optional): fix `migrate_paragraph_format.py` relpath convention and/or existing episode item descriptions to root-relative paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening an episode item whose `Key Files:` points at an existing `.podcast.md` renders the md viewer section in the detail view.
- [ ] Path-resolution regression test (red before the fix): a Key Files `.md` path resolves against the resolved worklog root (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` / `wlRoot`), and falls back to the `.llm-wiki/wiki/podcast/`-prefixed candidate when the root-relative path does not exist — covering the affected item's podcast-relative path.
- [ ] Existing chord/smart-selection/needsProducerReview behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Full plugin test suite passes (repo-root `npm test` = `vitest run`, covers `packages/herdr`) and `tsc` is clean.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `readKeyFile` (line ~2597) resolves Key Files paths against `process.cwd()`; must resolve against the worklog root with fallback candidates. Also `formatDetailContent` (line ~923), `renderFileViewer` (line ~1020), `firstMarkdownKeyFile` (line ~1040).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `configureWorklogTarget` (line ~293) / `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` (line ~339) / `wlRoot`; the resolved root must be threaded into `runWorklistTui` options so `readKeyFile` can use it.
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts` — `renderMarkdownViewer`, `renderNoteLinks` (md rendering helpers).
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.test.ts` — existing Key Files md viewer tests (injected `readFile`); extend for root/fallback resolution regression.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — TUI-level tests (chord/smart-selection/needsProducerReview guards; AC: unchanged behavior).
- External (open_source_llm worklog — NOT present on this machine, verify remotely): `.llm-wiki/wiki/podcast/irish-folklore-fine-tuning/irish-folklore-fine-tuning.podcast.md` (affected file), `migrate_paragraph_format.py` (relpath convention, lines ~472/533), `docs/pipeline-metadata-format.md` §2.7 (documented convention).

Related: WL-0MSGAEXER000707R (same class: plugin uses wrong CWD), OSL-0MSDYOVP6005T1X5 (md viewer feature), OSL-0MSG82DKE002LOYM (affected item).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-07 ~00:44 UTC: Plan pre-check (`plan-if-needed`) → decision **skip** (Effort: Extra Small, Risk: Low — see auto-plan decision comment WL-C0MSI7OZ2S007O3YU). Six automated review stages run against existing content; no child decomposition created. Changes: added fallback-resolution AC and path-resolution regression-test AC (Stage 1); added `## Key Files` section, external OSL paths marked as not mounted locally (Stage 2); clarified test command to repo-root `npm test`/`vitest run` + `tsc` (Stage 5). No clarifying questions needed — the description already had measurable ACs and a concrete fix; the optional data-side fix (open_source_llm) is out of scope for the plugin fix and not verifiable on this machine (OPEN QUESTION for the producer: whether to also run the optional data-side fix on the open_source_llm side).

**Summary**

The herdr shortcuts.json allows arbitrary variables in shortcut commands using the `<variable>` syntax (e.g. `/intake <description>`). Unknown variables trigger the Command Input form dialog.

**User story**

As a herdr user, I want shortcut command variables to support an inline default so that I can submit the form without typing a value for fields that have a sensible default.

**Expected behaviour**

- The syntax `<variable default=\"value\">` (single or double quotes) is supported in shortcuts.json commands.
- The Command Input form pre-fills the field with the default value; submitting without editing uses the default.
- The user can still edit/clear the field to override the default.
- Backwards compatible: variables without a default behave exactly as before (empty field).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `<priority default='medium'>` added to the `c` (create new) shortcut in packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json.
- [ ] `extractIdentifiers` / `getUnknownIdentifiers` return the default alongside the name.
- [ ] `FormState` pre-fills field values with defaults from the template.
- [ ] `substituteIdentifiers` falls back to the inline default when no explicit value is provided; explicit values take precedence.
- [ ] Unit tests cover extraction (double/single quotes), pre-fill, default submission, and override.

## Summary

`wl sync` fails on every push with `fatal: <path> already exists` because `withTempWorktree()` in `dist/sync.js` invokes `git worktree add --detach <tmp>/wt <ref>` **twice** — once inside a try/catch (added for the unborn-HEAD translation, SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51) and then unconditionally again right after the catch block. When the first call succeeds, the second always fails with "path already exists", aborting the sync.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In any repo with an initialized worklog and a remote (e.g. `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents` or `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`):
2. Run `wl sync` (or any push that triggers the pre-push hook).
3. Observe: `Sync failed: Command failed with exit code 128: git worktree add --detach '<repo>/.worklog/tmp-worktree-XXXXXX/wt' 'refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data'` → `fatal: '<...>/tmp-worktree-XXXXXX/wt' already exists`.

## Root cause

`/usr/local/lib/node_modules/worklog/dist/sync.js`, `withTempWorktree()`:

```js
try {
    await execAsync(`git worktree add --detach ...`);
}
catch (err) {
    // Unborn-HEAD translation (SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51) ...
    throw err;
}
await execAsync(`git worktree add --detach ...`);  // <- duplicate; fails when the first succeeded
```

The second call was likely meant to be the only call, or the catch should re-run only when the first call failed due to an unborn HEAD. Fix: remove the unconditional duplicate call while keeping the unborn-HEAD translation path working (covered by the SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51 tests).

## Impact

- All `wl sync` push operations fail in repos where the temp worktree can be created (the common case). Data is retained locally (SQLite + exported JSONL "retained for retry") but never pushed to the remote worklog ref.
- Blocks collaboration: other agents/operators do not see new work items, comments, effort/risk estimates.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl sync` succeeds and pushes to `refs/worklog/data` in a repo with a remote (regression test).
2. The unborn-HEAD translation error message still works: the single `git worktree add` call in `withTempWorktree()` remains wrapped with the unborn-HEAD translation (`src/sync.ts:937-951`), producing an actionable `Cannot sync: this repository has no commits yet...` message when a repo has no commits yet.

> **AC amendment (variance, 2026-08-07):** AC2 originally referenced `existing SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51 tests remain green`, but no such tests exist in the repo (verified by audit). The criterion is relaxed to verify the behavior directly in code: the translation logic is preserved and single-sourced around the one `git worktree add` call.

Discovered during WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 (discovered-from:WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8). The read-cache e2e tests (tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts) spawn the CLI via path.join(projectRoot, 'node_modules', '.bin', 'tsx'). implement.py start creates a fresh git worktree with NO node_modules, so in a worktree these 9 tests fail with 'Cannot find module <worktree>/node_modules/.bin/tsx' (node exits 1). This will fail implement.py finish for every future work item until the worktree gets node_modules.

**Confirmed**: all 9 e2e tests pass in the main checkout (node_modules present) and pass in a worktree after symlinking the root node_modules into it.

**Suggested fixes (pick one, decide ownership)**:
1. implement.py start symlinks/copies the repo root node_modules into the worktree (node_modules and .worklog are gitignored, so no repo pollution).
2. The e2e tests resolve tsx via an env var or the repo root path instead of projectRoot/node_modules.
3. Document that worktrees need a node_modules symlink.

## Resolution status (updated 2026-08-07 during plan)

Both suggested fixes 1 and 2 have already been implemented and verified; the failure mode described above is resolved:

1. **implement.py auto-symlink (suggested fix 1)** — shipped in SorraAgents work item SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B ("Auto-symlink node_modules into implement worktrees (implement.py start)", commit 03344c5c on dev). The shared skills (`~/.pi/agent/skills` -> `SorraAgents/skill`) now call `_ensure_node_modules_symlink()` right after `git worktree add` in `implement.py start`, creating `<worktree>/node_modules -> <repo-root>/node_modules` when the main checkout has one and the worktree lacks one. Live for ContextHub worktrees (an existing worktree, wl-WL-0MSI4TAT70058921, already carries the symlink).
2. **resolveTsxBin walk-up (suggested fix 2)** — shipped in ContextHub commit 613f1490 (2026-08-06): `tests/test-utils.ts` gained `resolveTsxBin()`, which walks up parent directories until it finds a real `node_modules/.bin/tsx`; all three read-cache test files (read-cache-e2e, read-cache-spawn-reduction, read-cache.test.ts) use it. From a worktree under `.worklog/worktrees/`, the walk reaches the main checkout's node_modules without any symlink.

**Verification (2026-08-07)**: ran `npx vitest run tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` in a fresh detached worktree at dev HEAD with NO node_modules and NO symlink — all 9 tests pass (37.5s). ## Summary

`wl next` (and `wl next -n <count>`) currently returns items whose stage is `done`, wasting fetch budget and polluting top-N work lists. Verified: `wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress` returned 20 items of which **12 had stage=done** (e.g. WL-0MMKENAJT14229DE, WL-0MMTDALZO0KQEZMI). Downstream consumers (herdr worklist `fetchNextItems`, pi TUI) then must filter them out client-side, and the TUI fetch budget is effectively reduced (herdr showed 9 items instead of 20 because 12 of the fetched 20 were done).

## User story

As an operator using wl next or a TUI that consumes it, I want done items excluded from results so that the top-N list is full of actionable work and no downstream filtering is needed.

## Expected behaviour

- `wl next` returns only non-done items by default (stage not in [done]).
- `wl next -n 20` returns up to 20 actionable items.
- The `--stage done` filter still allows explicitly requesting done items (filter semantics unchanged: stage filters remain explicit opt-in).
- Existing behaviour for other stages/statuses unchanged; dependency-blocked and in-progress handling unchanged.

## Implementation notes

- Likely in the `next` command implementation (src/commands/next.ts in ContextHub, which is also the global worklog CLI via npm link).
- Add an exclusion predicate for stage=done in the default (unfiltered) query path, similar to how status filters are applied.
- Check existing tests (tests/commands/next.test.ts or similar) and add coverage: a done item is excluded by default, included with explicit --stage done.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress` returns zero items with stage=done.
- [ ] `wl next --stage done -n 5` still returns done items.
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover the exclusion and the explicit --stage done opt-in.
- [ ] herdr worklist pane no longer needs its client-side stage=done filter (may be kept as defensive).

# Add Related Docs metadata row

## Summary

`buildMetaRows` gains a `Related Docs` row listing every `.md` path from the item's `Key Files:` section. Because `buildMetaRows` is shared, the row appears automatically in the list-mode metadata panel (`formatMetadataPanel`) and the detail-view metadata table (`formatDetailContent`). The panel row is display-only — activation/open-in-viewer lives in the detail-view ToC (see `Detail view ToC for Related Docs`).

## Expected behaviour

- Selecting a work item whose description has a `Key Files:` section with `.md` entries shows a `Related Docs` row with all markdown paths, compactly delimited and truncated to fit the row format.
- Items without `.md` Key Files show no `Related Docs` row (consistent with how `buildMetaRows` omits unset fields).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `buildMetaRows(item)` emits a `Related Docs` row whose value lists every `.md` path from `extractFilePaths(item.description)` (filter `endsWith('.md')`), joined with a compact delimiter (e.g. `, `).
2. The row is omitted when the item has no `.md` files in `Key Files:` or no `Key Files:` section at all.
3. The row renders correctly in both `formatMetadataPanel` output and the `formatDetailContent` metadata table via the shared builder; long values are truncated with the existing `truncateLine` and do not break the row layout.
4. The list-mode metadata panel row is display-only: no activation behavior is added there (per WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 Q1 answer: option C — opening happens in the detail-view ToC).
5. Display uses the paths as written in the description; no file I/O at render time. Resolution happens at open time via `resolveKeyFilePath` (resolved worklog root, never `process.cwd()`).

## Implementation approach

- Extend `buildMetaRows` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` with a `Related Docs` entry: `extractFilePaths(item.description)` filtered to `.md`, joined with `', '`, added via the existing `addMeta` helper (which omits empty values).

## Summary

Extend loadShortcutConfig() in packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts to accept an optional worklog root and merge <worklog-root>/shortcuts.json over the bundled defaults with local-wins override semantics. Bundled defaults remain the base; no bundled entries change.

## Context

Part of Extensible shortcuts.json: bundled defaults + project-local overrides (WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O). Local file location (decided): <worklog-root>/shortcuts.json — project root, version-controlled. Dedup key: view + chord; within the local file later entries win. Invalid local entries are validated with the existing parseShortcutEntry() and skipped with a logged error (never crash).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] loadShortcutConfig(worklogRoot?) loads bundled src/shortcuts.json first, then <worklogRoot>/shortcuts.json when it exists.
- [ ] A local entry with the same chord+view replaces the bundled entry; new local chords are appended; the resulting registry is deterministic with no duplicate entries.
- [ ] Invalid local entries are logged and skipped; a malformed local file (bad JSON / non-array) falls back to bundled-only with an error logged, never crashes.
- [ ] When no local file or no worklogRoot is supplied, the registry is byte-identical to today's bundled-only output.
- [ ] Code comments in shortcut-config.ts document the local file location and override semantics.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add optional worklogRoot parameter to loadShortcutConfig().
- Guarded read (existsSync + try/catch around readFileSync/JSON.parse) of <worklogRoot>/shortcuts.json.
- Parse local entries with the existing parseShortcutEntry().
- Merge via a Map keyed by view+chord (bundled first, then local entries overwrite/add), preserving bundled order for untouched entries; output a deduplicated array.

## Deliverables

- packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts changes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on Test-first: local-override merge tests (tests define the contract).

# Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime worker (`dispatchDowntimeWork` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) currently dispatches only two kinds of work during local-LLM idle time: `/skill:plan` on `intake_complete` items and `/skill:intake` on `idea` items. It never dispatches `/skill:audit` on `completed`/`in_review` items, so items sitting in the producer-review queue without a valid audit are never audited during downtime — despite the queue being the release gate (items are closed only after a valid audit shows "Ready to close: Yes").

## Users

- **Worklog operators / producers** — anyone who wants completed/in_review items automatically audited during local-LLM downtime so the review queue is drained and release readiness is known.
  - *User story:* "When my local LLM is idle, I want herdr to audit my completed/in_review items that lack a valid audit, so I don't have to manually run `/skill:audit` on each one."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the downtime worker is idle (per existing idle-detection), the first dispatch attempt targets a `completed`/`in_review` item **without a valid audit** — priority: audit tier before the existing plan/intake tiers.
2. "Valid audit" is defined by the herdr review-icon algorithm: the audit is *current* — i.e. the review icon is NOT the hourglass (⏳ stale passed) and NOT the magnifying glass (🔍 no audit / stale failed). Concretely: `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns `true` (auditedAt within the 60s staleness buffer of updatedAt).
3. The dispatched pane runs `/skill:audit <item-id>` (visible pane, `--no-focus`, named e.g. `Downtime audit`), following the existing `buildDowntimePaneArgs`/`spawnDowntimePane` pattern; the audit result persists via the audit skill's own lifecycle (no dispatch-side status changes needed beyond the existing claim pattern).
4. When no audit candidate exists, the worker falls back to the existing plan (`intake_complete`) then intake (`idea`) tiers, unchanged.
5. Dispatch audit trail: successful audit dispatches are recorded like other downtime dispatches (item comment + rolling `.worklog` downtime log) with kind `audit`.
6. Selection is deterministic and single-flight: at most one dispatch per idle period (existing tracker/`dispatchInFlight` behaviour); candidates are selected by sortIndex order like the heartbeat skill.
7. Tests cover: candidate selection (valid vs invalid audit), freshness boundary (60s buffer), audit-tier priority, fallback order, no-candidate handling, and dispatch audit logging.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments, README, and any relevant docs; CHANGELOG.md is managed by the ship skill and excluded).
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (pytest + Node, quiet mode).

## Constraints

- The downtime worker lives in the **Herdr plugin** (`packages/herdr/`); changes must follow the existing injectable-deps, fail-closed, single-flight patterns in `downtime-worker.ts`.
- Selection must reuse the existing `isAuditFresh` (or equivalent) freshness logic already present in `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — do not introduce a competing "valid audit" definition.
- Do NOT change the audit skill's freshness gate (`_check_audit_freshness` in SorraAgents) as part of this work — the dispatcher must select items whose audit is genuinely stale/missing so the runner's own gate falls through. (If a dispatched audit still hits "Skipping: audit still fresh", that's a separate issue to track.)
- The herdr review-icon algorithm (⏳/🔍) is the source of truth for "valid audit" — matches Q1 answer.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts) selects: (1) `wl next --stage intake_complete` → `/skill:plan <id>`, (2) fallback `wl next --stage idea` → `/skill:intake <id>`, else no dispatch. **No audit tier exists.**
- `getIconPrefix` (packages/herdr/src/icons.ts): for `in_review` items, fresh audit → ✅/❌/❓ based on `auditResult`; stale audit → ⏳ (if passed) or 🔍 (stage icon) — the 🔍/⏳ state is exactly "no valid audit".
- Heartbeat skill (`.pi/skills/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py`) audits completed/in_review items lacking "Ready to close: Yes" — but only when queue ≥ 10 items and only via one-off `/skill:heartbeat` invocations; sparse queues never audit, and fresh-but-failed audits get skipped by the runner's freshness gate.
- `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` returns auditResult/auditedAt/updatedAt (verified: 50 items today, 43 without audit).
- Audit runner (`_check_audit_freshness` in SorraAgents skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py): skips when `auditedAt > updatedAt + 60s`; otherwise runs a full audit. Items selected by the new tier (stale/missing audit) fall through this gate.

## Desired change

Add a third dispatch tier to the herdr downtime worker, **before** the existing plan/intake tiers:

1. Query completed/in_review items: `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json`.
2. Filter to items without a valid audit: `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)`.
3. Sort by `sortIndex` (like the heartbeat), take the first.
4. Claim the item (existing `claimItem` pattern) and spawn a pane running `/skill:audit <id>` via `buildDowntimePrompt('audit', candidate)` / `buildDowntimePaneArgs('audit', ...)`.
5. Extend `DowntimeSkillKind`/`DowntimeStage` types with `'audit'`, update `skillKindFromPrompt`, `buildDowntimePrompt`, pane naming, and the downtime-log event kind.
6. If no audit candidate: fall through to existing plan → intake tiers (unchanged).
7. Wire the new selection into `createDowntimeWorker` tick flow (same idle → dispatch path).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Freshness-gate interaction (assumption):** items selected by the new tier (stale/missing audit) fall through the audit runner's `_check_audit_freshness` gate (which only skips when `auditedAt > updatedAt + 60s`). If a dispatched audit still reports "Skipping: audit still fresh", that is a separate issue — do not modify the SorraAgents audit skill here.
- **`isAuditFresh` handles missing audit:** verified — `isAuditFresh` returns `false` when `auditedAt` or `updatedAt` is absent, so unaudited items are correctly selected.
- **Claim-before-dispatch for audits:** the existing `claimItem` (sets `status in_progress`) is applied before the pane spawns, consistent with the plan/intake tiers and the audit runner's own status lifecycle (runner demotes on "No", keeps `completed`/`in_review` on "Yes", restores on infra failure).
- **Scope-creep guard:** out of scope — changing the audit skill's freshness gate, adding audit-tier configuration, changing the heartbeat skill, or altering `wl next` selection semantics. Any such follow-ups get their own work items.
- **Model for audit pane:** dispatched audit panes use the configured downtime model (same as plan/intake), matching `buildDowntimePaneArgs` behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — add audit tier to `dispatchDowntimeWork`; extend types (`DowntimeSkillKind` + `'audit'`); new `getNextAuditCandidate` dep; update `buildDowntimePrompt`, `skillKindFromPrompt`, pane name.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps`: implement `getNextAuditCandidate` using `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` + `isAuditFresh` filter.
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — reuse `isAuditFresh` (no change expected; verify it handles the missing-audit case → returns false).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — audit event kind type if it restricts kinds.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — tests for selection, freshness, priority, fallback, logging.

## Related work

- **Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime (WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K)** — parent epic: downtime worker contract; this work extends it with the audit tier.
- **Log herdr downtime dispatches (WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8)** — dispatch audit trail; new audit events should follow the same pattern.
- **Same-slot idle tracking for herdr downtime worker (WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG)** — related idle-tracking refinement.
- **Heartbeat skill (WL-0MRIHB4Q100946QD)** — the manual/queue-gated audit path that this work complements.
- **Herdr plugin: eliminate the 'Other' group (WL-0MSAR110S002V26K)** — related worklist grouping.
- **Herdr worklist: render command input form (WL-0MSFZUS4Z006IRI3)** — related herdr UI work.
- **Rebuild wl next algorithm (WL-0MM2FKKOW1H0C0G4)** — selection queries rely on `wl next`/`wl list`; relevant if `wl next --stage in_review` behaviour affects candidate selection.
- **Extensible shortcut key system for Pi extension (WL-0MQD0YW40007RTKU)** — herdr shortcuts (`a a` audit chord) context.
- **Test: wl show includes audit summary (WL-0MPZNK1IC001JPTT)** — audit data exposure used by selection.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What counts as a 'valid audit' for this work?" — Answer (user@ContextHub): "if the herdr algorithm for showing the review icon says it is current (i.e. does not show the hour glass icon or the magnifying glass) then it is valid". Research: `getIconPrefix` in packages/herdr/src/icons.ts shows ⏳ (stale passed) or 🔍 (no audit / stale failed) exactly when `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)`; fresh audits show ✅/❌/❓. Source: interactive reply + packages/herdr/src/icons.ts.
- Q2: "What's the primary blocker you're hitting today?" — Answer (user@ContextHub): "I don't think the downtime dispatcher will select items ready for audit at all. If I am mistaken explain the existing algorithm." Research: confirmed — `dispatchDowntimeWork` selects only `intake_complete`→`/skill:plan` and `idea`→`/skill:intake`; there is no audit tier. The user was correct; the existing algorithm was documented in "Existing state". Source: interactive reply + packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts.
- Q3: "Where should the fix land?" — Answer (user@ContextHub): "the downtime detector and dispatcher in the Herdr plugin". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4 (follow-up): "Dispatch priority order — where should the audit tier sit?" — Recommendation (agent): audit first (completed/in_review items are release-critical). Answer (user@ContextHub): "agree". Source: interactive reply.


## Plan: features (plan skill, WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG)

Four child features, test-first (chain F0 → F1 → F2 → F3 via wl dep edges):

- **F0 — Audit-tier downtime dispatch tests** (WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV, task): extend `downtime-worker.test.ts` + `index.test.ts` for candidate selection, freshness boundary (60s), audit-tier priority, fallback order, no-candidate, dispatch audit logging (kind `audit`), and `getNextAuditCandidate` fail-closed parsing. Satisfies parent AC7/AC9.
- **F1 — Audit candidate selection** (WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31, feature): pure `parseAuditCandidatesOutput`/`selectAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`; filter `!isAuditFresh` (reuse `icons.ts`), sort ascending by `sortIndex`, first or null. Satisfies parent AC2/AC6.
- **F2 — Audit dispatch tier** (WL-0MSI9WPNI0044RL8, feature): extend `DowntimeSkillKind`/`DowntimeStage` with `audit`; add `getNextAuditCandidate` dep; dispatch audit → plan → intake; claim → spawn `/skill:audit <id>` (pane `Downtime audit`, `--no-focus`) → `recordDispatch` kind `audit`; kind-aware prompt/comment helpers. Satisfies parent AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5.
- **F3 — Wire audit tier and docs** (WL-0MSI9FXJH000GKIW, feature): `createDowntimeDeps.getNextAuditCandidate` runs `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` (fail-closed → null); README + code-comment updates; CHANGELOG.md excluded. Satisfies parent AC8/AC9.

Vertical-slice note: single small vertical slice (selection → dispatch → wiring → docs); no horizontal phasing required (effort Small). Between features, review and update the next item's description.

## Appendix: Planning session (WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG)

- Q5: "Approve the proposed feature plan (4 features, test-first, audit tier before plan/intake)?" — Answer (user@ContextHub): "lgtm" — approved as proposed. Evidence: interactive reply; plan recorded above. Final: accepted.

## Summary

Pure selection logic in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` that turns `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` output into the first stale/missing-audit candidate for the herdr downtime worker audit tier (parent WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG). Reuses `isAuditFresh` from `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` as the single source of truth for "valid audit".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` stdout (both array and `{workItems: [...]}` shapes) into typed audit candidates (id, title, auditedAt, updatedAt, sortIndex); malformed/empty output yields null (fail-closed).
- [ ] Filters to items WITHOUT a valid audit using `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` imported from `icons.ts` — no competing freshness definition is introduced.
- [ ] Missing `auditedAt` or `updatedAt` is selected (isAuditFresh returns false) — verified against `icons.ts`.
- [ ] Candidates are sorted ascending by `sortIndex` (heartbeat convention) and the first is returned; a fresh-audit-only result set yields null.
- [ ] **7-day recency filter**: candidates must have been modified within the last 7 days (`updatedAt` within `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS`). Items with a MISSING `updatedAt` are still included (recency cannot be verified → include, operator decision); items with an unparseable `updatedAt` are excluded (fail-closed). `selectAuditCandidate(candidates, now?)` takes an injectable clock for deterministic tests.
- [ ] Pure function(s) exported for unit testing; no wl CLI invocation inside the selection logic.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `AuditCandidate` interface (id, title, auditedAt?, updatedAt?, sortIndex?) and `parseAuditCandidatesOutput(stdout: string): AuditCandidate[] | null` in `downtime-worker.ts`.
- Add `selectAuditCandidate(candidates: AuditCandidate[], now = Date.now()): AuditCandidate | null` — filter `!isAuditFresh` AND 7-day recency (missing `updatedAt` included), sort by sortIndex ascending, return first.
- Add `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`.
- Import `isAuditFresh` from `./icons.js`; verify icons.ts needs no change (returns false for missing fields).

## Dependencies

- Parent: WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG. Prereq: F0 tests (WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV). Prereq of F2 (dispatch tier).

## Deliverables

- Exported selection helpers in `downtime-worker.ts`; unit tests green (F0).

# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.

## Summary

The herdr downtime worker dispatches work during local-LLM idle windows. `getNextItem` and `getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` run `wl` via `execFileAsync` with **NO timeout**, unlike `claimItem` (3s) and `recordDispatch` (5s). If a single `wl` invocation hangs, `dispatchDowntimeWork` never resolves: the worker's `dispatching` guard stays `true` forever and the scheduler's single-flight (`inFlight` never resets on a hung run) permanently stops the downtime task — **silently** (a hang is not a rejection, so no error is logged, no cooldown engages, and the pane stays open looking healthy).

## Evidence (2026-08-07)

- Pane 91's worker dispatched normally at 07:47/07:55/08:01/08:51/11:22Z, then **never dispatched again** until the pane exited at 15:58:29Z.
- The first post-dispatch idle threshold (~11:34Z, in the 6.1-min gap 11:34–11:40Z) aligns with the wedge onset; two plugin-origin pane splits at 11:39:31Z/11:40:06Z (grid-1) but **zero dispatch-log entries** — consistent with a wedged/in-flight attempt.
- The 24.3-min idle gap 15:18:06–15:42:26Z (lease-free for 23+ min, model loaded, audit-tier candidates available) produced no dispatch — pane 91's worker was dead the whole time.
- After the pane restart at 17:00Z, the new worker (pane 122) dispatched `/skill:audit LP-0MSI06HPB0043MV1` at 21:55:26Z on its first qualifying window — proving the code path is healthy when the worker is alive and that only pane restarts recover the wedge.
- `wl list`/`wl next` are fast (~0.15s) and healthy now; the hang was transient (no direct evidence preserved), but the missing timeouts make the failure mode a live, one-invocation-away risk.

## Fix direction

1. Add `timeout` to the `execFileAsync` calls in `getNextItem` / `getNextAuditCandidate` (e.g., 10s, matching the CLI's own 60s safety timeout as an upper bound) and surface the error via the existing error path (three-strike pause).
2. Add a scheduler-level watchdog: wrap the downtime task run with a timeout so a hung `run` resets `inFlight` (single-flight) instead of permanently blocking the tick loop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: `getNextItem` and `getNextAuditCandidate` wl invocations terminate after a bounded timeout on hang.
- [ ] AC2: A simulated hung `wl` does not permanently block the downtime task — the scheduler recovers on the next tick.
- [ ] AC3: Existing behavior unchanged: normal `wl` calls resolve with no added latency, successful dispatches still record to `downtime-dispatches.log` and claim via `wl update`.
- [ ] AC4: Tests cover the hang path (mock a never-resolving `wl`) and assert the task is not permanently wedged.

## Goal

Evaluate whether any herdr downtime worker that saw an idle window was actually enabled/configured to dispatch, and test the silent-failure paths (fail-closed candidate selection, claim conflict, spawn failure).

## Background

Hypotheses 3 & 4 from the RCA: (3) silent dispatch failure — `wl` failures/lock contention, candidate selection fail-closed (`wl next --stage` returns nothing), claim conflict, `send-to-pi.sh` spawn failure; (4) config/disablement — downtime worker disabled, paused (no-candidate cooldown), or dispatch window rules on the remote panes.

## Investigation steps

1. **Inspect herdr downtime worker configuration** on every pane that observed the idle window: enabled flag, dispatch window rules, no-candidate cooldown, proxy URL.

3. **Reproduce candidate selection fail-closed**: run `wl next --stage` with an empty/in-progress worklog to confirm behavior when no candidates exist.
4. **Check `send-to-pi.sh` spawn path**: any error swallowing that would silently drop a dispatch?

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Config state (enabled/disabled/paused/window rules) documented for every dispatch-capable pane that observed the idle window

# Dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection

**Summary:** Add a fail-safe read helper for the rolling dispatch log and exclude items the downtime worker has already dispatched for `/skill:audit` from audit-tier candidate selection (parent WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY, option A — dispatcher-scoped, no claim-path rework). Closes the re-selection loop where a dispatched audit run reverts the item to `completed`/`in_review` without a fresh audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `readDowntimeLogEntries(cwd)` returns `[]` on a missing or unreadable dispatch log and skips malformed JSONL lines without throwing (fail-safe — dispatch is never blocked by a log failure).
- [ ] `selectAuditCandidate` excludes candidates whose `itemId` has an audit-kind dispatch marker; composes with `isAuditFresh` (fresh audit → not a candidate, unchanged).
- [ ] `getNextAuditCandidate` loads the marker set from `<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (filtered to `kind === 'audit'`) and applies the exclusion; plan/intake tier selection is unchanged.
- [ ] All regression tests from WL-0MSLUANM5004NNPU pass; full project test suite green.
- [ ] Documentation updated: code comments (audit-tier selection contract), `packages/herdr/README.md` downtime section.

## Minimal Implementation

- `readDowntimeLogEntries(cwd)` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` (parse JSONL, skip malformed lines, missing/unreadable → `[]`, never throw).
- Optional exclusion parameter (e.g. `Set<string>` of audit-kind dispatched itemIds) on `selectAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — keeps the pure function deterministic and injectable.
- Wiring in `getNextAuditCandidate` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`): read log, build marker set, pass to selection; keep fail-closed semantics.

Prereq: WL-0MSLUANM5004NNPU (regression tests, test-first).

# Implement tier end-to-end in herdr downtime worker

## Summary

Add the `implement` dispatch tier to the herdr downtime worker: when idle, after the audit tier, dispatch `/skill:implement <id>` for the highest-priority open `plan_complete` item with risk `Low` and effort `Small`/`Extra Small`, excluding dependency-blocked items and already-dispatched markers. Falls back to plan/intake tiers when no implement candidate exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `DowntimeStage`/`DowntimeSkillKind` extended with `'implement'`; `skillKindFromPrompt` and `buildDowntimePrompt` map the implement kind to `/skill:implement <id>`; dispatched pane named e.g. `Downtime implement` via the existing `buildDowntimePaneArgs`/`spawnDowntimePane` pattern (`--no-focus`, visible pane).
2. New `createDowntimeDeps.getNextImplementCandidate(cwd)` dep runs `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk low --effort small -n N --json` (N generous), filters client-side to `status === 'open'`, excludes dispatched markers (kind `implement`, `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`), and returns the first candidate in wl next's priority order; fail-closed → `null` on `wl` CLI error or empty result.
3. `dispatchDowntimeWork` runs the implement tier after the audit tier and before the plan/intake tiers; when the implement tier yields no candidate or errors, the worker falls back to the existing plan (`intake_complete`) then intake (`idea`) tiers unchanged.
4. Dispatch order is audit → implement → plan → intake; audit stays first as the release gate.
5. Successful implement dispatches record a `kind: implement` event through the existing dispatch audit trail (item comment + rolling `.worklog` downtime log); no dispatch-side status/stage changes beyond the existing pre-dispatch claim pattern (`claimItem`, idempotent with `implement.py start`'s own claim).
6. Selection is deterministic and single-flight: at most one dispatch per idle period (existing tracker/`dispatchInFlight`); a `wl next` CLI error at the implement tier does NOT short-circuit the plan/intake fallback (mirrors existing tier-2-error handling).
7. Docs updated: code comments in `downtime-worker.ts`/`index.ts` and the herdr README describe the implement tier and its dispatch order (CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship skill).
8. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (pytest + Node, quiet mode).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — implement tier in `dispatchDowntimeWork`; extend `DowntimeStage`/`DowntimeSkillKind`; prompt/pane naming; implement-tier CLI-error fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps.getNextImplementCandidate`: `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk low --effort small -n N --json` (fail-closed → null) + status=open + dispatched-marker exclusion.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — `implement` event kind if it restricts kinds.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — dispatch tier documentation.

- Blocked-by: WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG (wl next `--risk`/`--effort` filters) and WL-0MSMAYIKX005LLO4 (test-first test matrix).
- Consumes: `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk low --effort small` (delivered by WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG).
- Fallback if the child lands late: `wl next --stage plan_complete -n N --json` + client-side risk/effort/status filtering (still priority-ordered and blocked-excluded); record which path was taken.

- Parent: Dispatch low-risk work items from plan_complete stage (WL-0MSM9HEH8001A55I)
- Prerequisite: Add risk/effort filters to wl next and convert herdr downtime dispatch selection to wl next (WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG)

## Problem statement

The worklist test suite is a 7,073-line monolith that covers all worklist
functionality — state, formatting, mouse input, key handling, rendering, TUI
integration, hydration, etc. Navigating and editing one concern requires holding
thousands of unrelated tests in view.

## Goal

Break the test file into cohesive modules so no file exceeds 1,000 lines.
